commits.pr_title: [Perf][Attention] Vectorize per-token-head KV tile loads in Triton attention
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Triton attention kernels read per-token-head KV caches (`int4_per_token_head`, `int8_per_token_head`, `fp8_per_token_head`) one byte per load instruction. This PR works out, from the actual strides and offsets of the cache at launch, the widest alignment the compiler can rely on, and the kernels then load that many bytes per instruction, prefetched. At head size 128, for example, K is read 8 bytes and V 4 bytes at a time instead of 1.

Only the generated kernel code changes. The KV cache memory layout, page size and memory use stay as they are, so this is independent of, and compatible with, the open PRs that change the layout (#62113, #56164). Same root cause as #56081.

## Claims

- **Serving throughput goes up** for the per-token-head KV dtypes on `TRITON_ATTN`. `vllm bench serve`, total token throughput, mean of two runs per build, main -> this PR (terminal output below):
  - Qwen3-14B, int8, A100: 3536 -> 4701 tok/s (+33%) on 8192-token prefill, 2970 -> 3995 tok/s (+34%) with 256-token decode.
  - Qwen3-14B, int4, A100: 3641 -> 4214 tok/s (+16%) on 8192-token prefill, 3141 -> 3691 tok/s (+18%) with 256-token decode.
  - Qwen3-8B, int8, A100: 5586 -> 7624 tok/s (+36%) on 8192-token prefill, 4472 -> 6300 tok/s (+41%) with 256-token decode.
  - Qwen3-8B, int4, A100: 5822 -> 6386 tok/s (+10%) on 8192-token prefill, 4799 -> 5333 tok/s (+11%) with 256-token decode.
  - Qwen3-0.6B, fp8, RTX 5060 Ti: 9462 -> 13958 tok/s (+48%) on 8192-token prefill, 5884 -> 8730 tok/s (+48%) with 256-token decode.
- **Accuracy is unchanged**: `lm_eval` GSM8K, of the 16 main/PR score pairs, 14 differ by no more than the reported stderr. The largest gap is -0.0228 (Qwen3-0.6B fp8); a repeat of both builds gives +0.0083, and two runs of the same build differ by up to 0.0159 (terminal output below).
- **Kernel output is bit-identical to main**: with the same inputs, the raw output bytes have the same sha256 on main and on this PR for every kernel call checked (72 on the RTX 5060 Ti, 48 on the A100), including the engine's interleaved layout, where main loads byte by byte and this PR 8 and 4 bytes at a time.
- **Small diff**: +78 -1 in 3 files, test included.
- **No layout, page-size or memory change, and no new option.** The default (bf16) KV cache takes the unchanged code path.

## Validation

Builds: main `cc00267752`, this PR `bb50346e57`. The head is now `a5434a359a`, which only adds the K base address to `kv_tile_alignment` (review feedback): for the 16-byte-aligned base the engine passes it returns the same values and the compiled kernels are identical, so the runs below were not repeated. Machines: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB (SM 8.0) and, for fp8, an RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB (SM 12.0, WSL2); FP8 KV with the Triton backend needs SM 8.9 or newer, so the A100 cannot run it on either build. Every block below is the terminal output of the command printed above it. Each server was started from its own source tree. The `# main` logs are from Nov 21-22 and the `# Now` logs from Nov 23, after the diff was shrunk, on the same two machines; the first revision of this PR (`95dc7eda0b`), run interleaved with main (main, PR, PR, main), compiles to the same kernels and gave the same throughput within 1.6% in every run:

```bash
# in the main checkout, then in the PR checkout
python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve <model> --kv-cache-dtype <dtype> --port 8011
```

On the RTX 5060 Ti the server also had `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.6`, because WSL2 shares the card with the desktop. The benchmark commands also carried `--save-result --result-dir <dir> --result-filename <name>`, and `lm_eval` carried `--output_path <dir>`.

### Accuracy: `lm_eval`, GSM8K

`num_concurrent=64` instead of the 1024 of the review example: with one GPU, requests queued behind 1024 concurrent ones can run into `lm_eval`'s 300 s request timeout. The value changes how requests are batched, not what is evaluated. Scores also move a little between two runs of the same build, because batching depends on timing (fp8 below was run twice per build). For Qwen3-14B, `lm_eval` ran on the first server of each build right after the two benchmark workloads; for the other models on servers of their own.

### Other checks

- Unit tests: the per-token-head and Triton attention kernel tests pass on this PR; commands and pytest summary lines are in the supplementary material.
- `test_triton_unified_attention_per_token_head_scale` gains one parameter, `interleaved`: K/V in one buffer with a 4-byte scale slot after each (the engine layout, where the wider loads are used). With a deliberately doubled K or V alignment exactly these new cases fail and the separate-tensor cases still pass.
- Bit-identical output is checked outside the test suite, see "Bit-identical kernel output" in the supplementary material.
- A K/V buffer starting 1, 4 or 8 bytes into its allocation runs without error and gives the same output bytes as an aligned one (RTX 5060 Ti; int4, int8, fp8): Triton compiles such launches with byte loads, at `bb50346e57` and at this head alike. Raw output is in the review thread.
- On the first revision (`95dc7eda0b`), the kernel JIT monitor reported the same compilations as main and `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` passed on both builds (A100, int8). Not repeated at this head, which compiles to the same kernels.

## Details

**Why it is slow today.** Triton only learns from an argument whether it is a multiple of 16. A per-token-head cell is `[K | k_scale (4 B) | V | v_scale (4 B)]`, 136 bytes for int4 and 264 bytes for int8/fp8 at head size 128, so the stride between cells and the V base pointer carry no such flag. The compiler then cannot prove any alignment and emits one load per byte, which is also too narrow to be turned into a prefetched async copy.

**What changes.** The alignment that does hold is computed from the tensors, not assumed.

- `kv_tile_alignment(k, v)` runs at launch and returns the greatest power of two, up to 16, that divides every K stride, and the one that divides every V stride and the offset of V from K. For head size 128 these are 8 and 4 bytes; other head sizes get whatever their strides allow.
- At its top, each of the two kernels rewrites each stride as `stride // ALIGN * ALIGN` (same value, but now visibly a multiple of the constexpr `ALIGN`) and addresses V from the K pointer. Triton can then prove the alignment and emit loads of that width.
- Used by the int4 kernel and by the unified kernel for int8/fp8 per-token-head. Every other dtype passes `ALIGN = 1`, which leaves the addressing exactly as before. The tensor-descriptor path (`USE_TD`) is not touched.

**Compatibility with open PRs.** #62113 pads the int8/fp8 cell to 16 bytes (more KV memory per token, int4 unchanged); #56164 adds an opt-in mode with scales in separate tensors. This PR does not touch the layout, so it neither depends on nor conflicts with either: if the cells become multiples of 16, `kv_tile_alignment` returns 16, which is what Triton's own flags already give. #56081 reports the same root cause for a gather-based sparse kernel, which is not changed here.

**Limitations.**

- Measured on NVIDIA only. I could not run AMD or Intel; on XPU the unified kernel loads K/V through tensor descriptors, where this is off.
- fp8 was measured on the 16 GB RTX 5060 Ti only, so with a small model.
- The gain relies on Triton proving `x // c * c` divisible by `c` (checked on Triton 3.8.0). If that stops, the loads fall back to byte loads and results stay correct.
- `tests/models/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py` needs the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`, which I could not download.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write the change, run the measurements and draft this description.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix /classify for per-position seq-cls heads on the Transformers backend
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix `/classify` on the Transformers modeling backend for sequence classification heads that are applied at every position, which returned `(num_seqs, 1, num_labels)` and failed with `pooled_data should be a 1-D probability vector`.

## Claims

- `nn.Linear` heads (BERT's `classifier`, CTRL's `classifier`, and the `score` heads of Llama, Mistral, Qwen2, ... once #67018 lets them load) skip `ClassifierWithReshape` and return `(num_seqs, num_labels)`.
- Non-`nn.Linear` heads applied at every position (LayoutLMv3's and Funnel's `*ClassificationHead`) have the extra dim squeezed back out.
- Heads that select their own token (the 22 `features[:, 0, :]`-style `*ClassificationHead` classes, e.g. RoBERTa's) and `num_labels=1` `/score` results are unchanged.

## Details

The pooler has already extracted one hidden state per sequence. `ClassifierWithReshape` unsqueezes it to `(num_seqs, 1, hidden)` because heads like RoBERTa's index `features[:, 0, :]`, but it was applied to every classifier, so any head that runs at every position kept the extra dim. The fix only wraps non-`nn.Linear` heads, and the wrapper squeezes 3-D outputs for the few of those that are applied at every position.

## Validation

Output shapes of each head on CPU with tiny random configs and a `(2, 64)` input, using this branch's wrapping logic:

| Head | Wrapped | Output |
|---|---|---|
| CTRL `nn.Linear` | no | `(2, 3)` |
| BERT `nn.Linear` | no | `(2, 3)` |
| RoBERTa `RobertaClassificationHead` | yes | `(2, 3)` |
| Funnel `FunnelClassificationHead` | yes | `(2, 3)` |
| LayoutLMv3 `LayoutLMv3ClassificationHead` | yes | `(2, 3)` |

End to end, the tiny CTRL classifier was served on the earlier revision of this fix (squeeze-only, same output for `nn.Linear` heads), and @taneem-ibrahim reproduced it on `main` on an H100:

```python
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, CTRLConfig, CTRLForSequenceClassification

torch.manual_seed(0)
config = CTRLConfig(vocab_size=32000, n_embd=64, n_layer=2, n_head=4, dff=128, num_labels=3)
CTRLForSequenceClassification(config).save_pretrained("/tmp/tiny-ctrl-cls")
AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("vllm-project/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM").save_pretrained("/tmp/tiny-ctrl-cls")
```

```bash
vllm serve /tmp/tiny-ctrl-cls --model-impl transformers --runner pooling
curl -s localhost:8000/classify -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model": "/tmp/tiny-ctrl-cls", "input": ["The food here is delicious", "You are a wonderful person"]}'
```

| | probs |
|---|---|
| Before | `400: pooled_data should be a 1-D probability vector` |
| After | `[[0.3682, 0.3136, 0.3182], [0.3851, 0.2914, 0.3235]]` |
| Transformers | `[[0.3683, 0.3135, 0.3182], [0.3851, 0.2914, 0.3236]]` |

Unchanged by the fix: `vllm-project/xlm-roberta-base-language-detection` `/classify` (RoBERTa head) and `/score` with the same CTRL classifier at `num_labels=1` (`[0.56429, 0.55918]`).

No duplicate open PR or issue: #67018 fixes loading `score` weights, not the output shape, and touches a different part of `pooling.py`.

AI assistance was used to investigate, write the fix, and draft this description. The `nn.Linear` gate and the shape checks above were added in a follow-up by a maintainer, also with AI assistance.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][MM] Use varlen attention in MiniCPM-V vision encoder
commits.pr_body:
## Overview
This PR replaces masked SDPA with variable-length attention for padded batches in MiniCPM-V’s eager vision encoder.

MiniCPM-V/O batches image slices with different patch counts by padding them to a common length and using masked PyTorch SDPA. In a timing-only test on MiniCPM-V 4.6 with 500 synthetic prompts and 8 images per prompt (mixed 448×448 and 336×672), setting attention_mask=None switched the encoder to batched MMEncoderAttention. Mean encoder forward time fell by 15.5% with padding still in place, pointing to the attention path is an opportunity for optimization.

This PR uses variable-length MMEncoderAttention for padded batches in the eager vision encoder. It packs valid patches and uses cu_seqlens to keep attention within each slice.



## Claims
### Results
- On the mixed-resolution `vllm bench mm-processor` workload, mean `encoder_forward_ms` decreased by 26.5% for MiniCPM-V 4.0 and 15.6% for MiniCPM-V 4.6.
- ChartQA relaxed accuracy changed by −0.16 and +0.48 percentage points, respectively. Both changes were smaller than the reported standard errors.

### Changes
- Attention goes through `MMEncoderAttention` with `cu_seqlens` / `max_seqlen`, e.g. `flash_attn_varlen_func` on the FlashAttention backend. Backend-specific metadata is prepared with the existing `MMEncoderAttention` helpers (`maybe_recompute_cu_seqlens`, `compute_max_seqlen`, `maybe_compute_seq_lens`), the same way as Qwen-VL.
- Valid patch tokens are packed into a single sequence `(1, N, D)`, and `cu_seqlens` marks the slice boundaries (block-diagonal attention).
- Outputs are unpacked back to the padded layout, so downstream modules (resampler / merger) are unchanged.

### Scopes
- `Idefics2VisionTransformer.forward` gets an opt-in `use_varlen` flag (default `False`), so Idefics3, Phi-4-MM and the MiniCPM-V encoder CUDA graph path keep their current behavior.
- MiniCPM-V 2.5 / 2.6 / 4.0 / 4.5 (and MiniCPM-O 2.6 / 4.5 via inheritance) enable it in their eager `get_vision_hidden_states`.
- MiniCPM-V 4.6 / 4.7 run the encoder layers directly (with the ViT merger inserted mid-encoder), so they build the varlen metadata before and after the merger.
- Batches without padding use regular batched attention.



## Validation
### Test Plan
**Test Scope**: MiniCPM-V 4.0 and 4.6, before and after
**Device**: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090
**MM Encoder Attn Backend**: FLASH_ATTN


**Accuracy**: ChartQA
```bash
lm_eval \
  --model vllm-vlm \
  --model_args "pretrained=/root/autodl-tmp/models/MiniCPM-V-4_6,gpu_memory_utilization=0.9,trust_remote_code=True" \
  --tasks chartqa \
  --apply_chat_template \
  --batch_size auto
```
**Performance**: vllm bench mm-processor
```bash
vllm bench mm-processor \
  --model /root/autodl-tmp/models/MiniCPM-V-4_6 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --dataset-name random-mm \
  --num-prompts 500 \
  --num-warmups 100 \
  --max-model-len 4096 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --seed 42 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \
  --random-mm-base-items-per-request 8 \
  --random-mm-num-mm-items-range-ratio 0.0 \
  --random-mm-bucket-config '{"(448, 448, 1)": 0.5, "(336, 672, 1)": 0.5}'
```

### Test Results
#### Accuracy
**ChartQA (relaxed_accuracy, within stderr)**
| Model | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| MiniCPM-V 4.0 | 0.8376 ± 0.0074 | 0.8360 ± 0.0074 |
| MiniCPM-V 4.6 | 0.4488 ± 0.0099 | 0.4536 ± 0.0100 |

The relatively low ChartQA accuracy of MiniCPM-V-4.6 may be partly attributed to its smaller 0.8B language backbone. Additionally, I run a test with `--log_samples`. The `--log_samples` output showed cases where MiniCPM-V 4.6 identified the correct value but lost credit because of the answer format. For example, Final Answer: There are 14 food items shown in the bar graph. was scored as incorrect for a reference answer of 14.

commits.pr_title: [Recipes][XPU] Add validated 8192-token context defaults for some Qwen, Nemotron-3-Nano,  and GPT-OSS models on Arc Pro B60/B70
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Align vLLM Recipes with documented Intel Arc Pro B60/B70 serving configurations by adding hardware- and variant-specific `--max-model-len 8192` defaults across 10 model recipes.

These overrides provide practical context-length defaults for XPU deployments and address KV-cache capacity issues observed during B70 validation.

## Claims

- Add 8192-token defaults for six Qwen BF16 recipes on Arc Pro B60/B70:
  - Qwen3-32B
  - Qwen3.5-9B
  - Qwen3.5-27B
  - Qwen3.5-35B-A3B
  - Qwen3.6-27B
  - Qwen3.6-35B-A3B
- Address KV-cache capacity failures on B70 for:
  - Qwen3-32B-AWQ
  - Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4
  - Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct BF16
- Extend documented 8192-token XPU defaults to:
  - GPT-OSS-20B (MXFP4)
  - Nemotron-3-Nano-4B (BF16/FP8)
  - Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B (BF16/FP8)
- Cover both B60 and B70 for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct BF16.
- Preserve existing hardware-specific arguments and configurations for other accelerators.
- Reuse the existing Recipes schema without changes to vLLM runtime or Recipes tooling.

## Validation

- Reviewed the existing Intel Arc Pro B60/B70 serving configurations documented in the affected Recipes.
- B70 weekly validation confirmed that Qwen3.5-9B BF16 successfully serves with `--max-model-len 8192`.
- B70 validation identified KV-cache capacity failures for Qwen3-32B-AWQ, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4, and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct at their original context lengths.
- Verified the YAML override structure and patch application against the corresponding source sections.
- Full schema validation, generated-command checks, and end-to-end runtime validation for all affected model/variant/hardware combinations remain pending.

## Details

Several Intel Arc Pro B60/B70 Recipes document `--max-model-len 8192` in their deployment guides, but the setting was not consistently represented in the structured recipe configuration. As a result, generated serving commands could request the model's much larger native context length and exceed the available KV-cache capacity.

This PR adds the context-length setting through the existing `variants.<variant>.hardware_overrides` mechanism:

```yaml
hardware_overrides:
  arc_pro_b60:
    extra_args:
      - "--max-model-len"
      - "8192"
  arc_pro_b70:
    extra_args:
      - "--max-model-len"
      - "8192"
```

The overrides are intentionally scoped to the applicable hardware and model variants. The AWQ and GPTQ KV-cache workarounds apply only to B70, while the documented serving defaults for the other included variants cover both B60 and B70.

The change preserves model-native context-length metadata, existing XPU runtime arguments, and hardware overrides for other platforms. It does not introduce a global XPU context-length policy.

The 8192-token setting is a practical serving default, not an architectural limit. Users can increase the context length when sufficient KV-cache capacity is available.

## Overview

Bound per-prompt media preprocessing allocations with `VLLM_MAX_MEDIA_PREPROCESSING_BYTES` (default 715,827,880 bytes, about 683 MiB). This limit is independent of the request download and decode budgets. Requests that exceed a supported processor's estimate return HTTP 400.

This PR consolidates #68375 (FunAudioChat), #68767 (Nano Nemotron VL), and #68898 (DeepSeek-VL2 and OCR), together with Molmo2 image crops and the Qwen3-VL, LLaVA-OneVision, Gemma 4, and EmbeddingGemma2 video paths. The three source PRs are closed as superseded. It addresses [the consolidation request](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69098#issuecomment-7059883576) and incorporates the multi-page OCR and compile-cache follow-ups from #68898.

## Behavior

- FunAudioChat estimates padded raw audio, spectrum buffers, and feature tensors before feature extraction. The byte-derived item cap applies to waveforms; precomputed `audio_embeds` retain the configured item limit.
- Nano Nemotron VL, DeepSeek-VL2, and Molmo2 estimate image tiles and temporary tensors before materializing them. DeepSeek-OCR and Unlimited-OCR count all document views and tiles plus one view's temporary buffers.
- Qwen3-VL, LLaVA-OneVision, Gemma 4, and EmbeddingGemma2 count video pixel tensors retained across clips. The processors that concatenate those tensors also count the additional output buffer while the inputs remain live.
- Qwen3-VL and LLaVA-OneVision default to at most 32 videos per prompt and honor an explicit `--limit-mm-per-prompt.video`. Operators can configure the byte limit independently of that count and the decode limit.
- Accepted raw-media preprocessing outputs are unchanged; the change affects admission of over-budget requests. This follow-up also makes FunAudioChat's precomputed `audio_embeds` path usable when enabled.

## Validation

### Final CI

[Buildkite #105407](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/105407) passed on the final PR head, `c22a3478b06c`. All multimodal processor shards passed on CPU, AMD MI355, and NVIDIA H200. The OpenAI API completion jobs and the test coverage check also passed.

The change merged into `main` as `880c63222bbf`.

The consolidated audio, image, OCR, and Qwen/LLaVA video work passed 23 focused tests on macOS arm64 CPU before the Gemma follow-up. Those tests cover budget boundaries, multi-page OCR, processor cache behavior, item-count overrides, and the real render endpoint:

```sh
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_launch_render.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_video_budget.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_funaudiochat.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/test_nano_nemotron_vl.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_deepseek_vl2.py \
  -k 'preprocessing_budget or over_budget or default_ocr_budget or video_item_limit_defaults or max_audio_samples_match_profiled' \
  --tb=short
```

For Gemma 4, the render regression sends two distinct four-frame 128×128 videos with a 6 MiB preprocessing limit. On pre-fix commit `1d624651d15d8490e942090599f0a8dc8b4598a2`, the combined request returned HTTP 200 and the test failed its expected-400 assertion (`1 failed, 30 deselected`). On fixed commit `d5a602fc2a4c1d78f865b77468bef18eff48b094`, the combined request returned HTTP 400 and either video alone returned HTTP 200 (`1 passed, 30 deselected`). Six existing Gemma 4 video placeholder and processor-cache tests also passed (`6 passed, 44 deselected`). The focused command is:

```sh
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_launch_render.py \
  -k 'rejects_over_budget_video_tensors and gemma' -q --tb=short
```

The local worktree used a temporary CLI wrapper and package metadata because its shared virtual environment did not have an installed `vllm` entry point. Changed-file pre-commit hooks passed, including ruff, mypy, and Buildkite test wiring; `git diff --check` passed. The EmbeddingGemma2 checkpoint was unavailable locally, so that path did not get a model-backed run. GPU generation and full-checkpoint accuracy evaluation were outside these CPU validation runs.

### Review follow-up at `9282578dde`

The image preprocessing checks now skip internal profiling inputs through the shared `profiling_media()` context, while request processing still enforces the configured budget. Video frame, size, and embedding options now retain the 32-video default unless the operator explicitly sets a count.

On the previous PR head `d4b764c581`, `test_profiling_dummy_image_ignores_request_budget` failed with `Image preprocessing exceeds VLLM_MAX_MEDIA_PREPROCESSING_BYTES=1`; the video count regression failed for both Qwen3-VL and LLaVA-OneVision because 33 items were accepted. On `9282578dde`:

```text
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH=<review worktree> .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/config/test_multimodal_config.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_deepseek_vl2.py tests/models/multimodal/test_nano_nemotron_vl.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_video_budget.py -k 'multimodal_config or image_preprocessing_budget or profiling_dummy_image or static_image_preprocessing_budget or video_item_limit_defaults' -q --tb=short
100 passed, 66 deselected, 2 warnings in 11.31s
```

The `RemoteLaunchRenderServer` regression used a temporary local `vllm` launcher and package metadata:

```text
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH=<review worktree>:<temporary metadata> .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_launch_render.py -k video_options_keep_default_count_limit -q --tb=short
1 passed, 31 deselected, 1 warning in 10.78s
```

All commit hooks passed, including mypy and the Buildkite test wiring check. These are CPU render and processor checks; GPU inference and model accuracy evaluation remain unrun for this follow-up.
After `/ci run` merged current `main` as `8dcbe81beaf4`, I reran both commands on that head: 100 focused tests passed in 12.41s, and the render-endpoint regression passed in 10.74s.

### Molmo2 follow-up at `001b69078d191d691cb016e4eb1b4c6a547f91d0`

Molmo2's image processor could allocate all tiled float32 crops and their concatenated copy before prompt-length validation, while the decoded-media budget charged only the original image pixels. The new check estimates the actual tiling from each image's dimensions and the effective crop settings, totals the crop bytes across the prompt, and rejects over-budget requests before calling the HF processor. An accepted single-image request still renders normally. This extends the shared budget introduced in this PR; #68767 covered a different model and did not fix Molmo2.

The new regressions failed on the previous PR head `6e94efc47990f7106d5285e96107062e89059648`: the processor test reported `Failed: DID NOT RAISE VLLMValidationError` (`1 failed, 12 deselected, 4 warnings in 5.54s`), and the render endpoint returned HTTP 200 where the test expected HTTP 400 (`1 failed, 12 deselected, 3 warnings in 14.75s`). On `001b69078d191d691cb016e4eb1b4c6a547f91d0`, with the local CLI wrapper and package metadata described above:

```sh
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH=<PR worktree>:<temporary metadata> \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_molmo2.py -q --tb=short
```

```text
13 passed, 12 warnings in 17.73s
```

Changed-file pre-commit hooks passed, including ruff, mypy, and Buildkite test wiring. The regression uses `allenai/Molmo2-8B` processor files on macOS arm64 CPU; no model weights or GPU inference were loaded. The change only rejects requests above the preprocessing limit and does not modify accepted processor outputs.

### Review fixes at `3002ade5b3`

The 32-video default is now documented for every processor family that inherits `Qwen3VLProcessingInfo`. The Molmo2 estimate also skips disabled and profiling budgets before reading image dimensions, and uses `ImageProcessorItems.get_image_size` for CHW tensors and HWC arrays. The prior Molmo2 size helper asserted on CHW tensors; the CHW regression failed on `aedb7d371f` with an uncaught `AssertionError` for both enabled and disabled budgets. On `3002ade5b3`, the inputs reach the Hugging Face processor's normal validation path:

```sh

```

```text
16 passed, 1 deselected, 15 warnings in 5.03s
```

Changed-file pre-commit hooks passed, including ruff, mypy, and Buildkite test wiring. The array cases are CPU processor tests; the render endpoint regression above was last run on `001b69078d`.

### FunAudioChat and DeepSeek-OCR review follow-up at `bc171da3fc`

The waveform estimate no longer sets FunAudioChat's shared modality count, which also applies to `audio_embeds`. A representation-aware admission check now counts raw audio before processor-cache reuse, and the processor retains a count guard for direct callers. Precomputed embeddings use `--limit-mm-per-prompt` and bypass the waveform feature extractor. The processor and model now carry those embeddings through to their token placeholders and output.

With a 500,000-byte preprocessing budget and a configured two-audio limit, the new `/v1/chat/completions/render` test sends two serialized one-token `audio_embeds`. On previous head `3002ade5b3`, it returned HTTP 400 (`At most 1 audio(s)`); on `bc171da3fc`, it returns HTTP 200 with two audio placeholders. The same endpoint rejects two raw audio items with HTTP 400, including when both use the same URL and the processor cache can reuse one result. Profiling inputs bypass this request budget. The full FunAudioChat test file passed: **8 passed** on macOS arm64 CPU with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH=<PR worktree> PATH=<temporary CLI wrapper>:$PATH .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_funaudiochat.py -q --tb=short`. Changed-file hooks passed, including ruff, mypy, Markdown, and CI test wiring.

For DeepSeek-OCR output parity, I ran the processor on base commit `d6d1616c1c` and PR head `3002ade5b3` with three distinct generated RGB pages (8×8, 64×32, 32×64), each with different per-pixel channel patterns. Both `v1` and `v2` produced exactly identical `input_ids`, `pixel_values`, `images_crop`, `images_spatial_crop`, `images_seq_mask`, and `num_image_tokens`. The three global views and four local crops each had distinct SHA-256 hashes, so the comparison exercised page and tile ordering. The whole-tensor hashes matched across revisions: `pixel_values` `b7030e7454fcd1e5d0d793af4797cd8de911fc0bcd83f67d97ca1b74a9cb9d05`, `images_crop` `02b8faaf01dc182cfecb92b15d4e269deab978a3417eeabba70d3e069b14bcd3`, and `images_spatial_crop` `0e76ebff9316312393bc08b8872267f6a00a4757ce5333258510c9885704a442`. The image-mask hashes also matched for each strategy (`d420b622997f78a73d9fb81a263b2dbafd714d89e0ce06fc2061479ddaa53cde` for `v1`, `1baa31cf04b6119ed55e251df30f27a08d829821091476fab7be06ad02c3e230` for `v2`). Four focused DeepSeek image-budget tests passed; the full OCR suites could not run offline because their model files are not cached. No GPU model output evaluation was run for this follow-up.

### Video kwargs review follow-up at `1c7b97ea16`

LLaVA-OneVision now estimates video resize and crop geometry using the same resolved Hugging Face options as preprocessing. Qwen3-VL uses the effective patch, merge, and temporal patch sizes for resize geometry and frame padding. Both keep the actual-byte check. The change also documents when `default_mm_limits` applies.

On the previous PR head `70e836fb3b`, the new LLaVA render regression returned HTTP 400 for the small clip with resizing disabled (`1 failed, 1 warning in 12.61s`). On `1c7b97ea16`, disabling resize or supplying a smaller size returns HTTP 200. Default resizing still returns a budget error and malformed options return HTTP 400. The focused CPU render suite ran with all three models' cached processor assets:


Both Qwen3-VL cases failed the old preflight on `70e836fb3b` (`2 failed, 17 deselected, 1 warning in 6.66s`). The matching spatial and temporal overrides now produce the expected patch grids and fit exactly within the byte budget:


The multimodal configuration and kwargs checks also passed (`100 passed, 105 deselected, 1 warning in 13.53s`), as did the changed-file commit hooks, including mypy and Buildkite test wiring. These runs validate CPU rendering and preprocessing. GPU generation and model accuracy were outside this follow-up's validation.

### Preprocessing budget audit follow-up at `6343baa932`

- Nano Nemotron VL checks dynamic resize targets before CPU resize or device staging. Molmo2 returns HTTP 400 for incomplete image resize options and preserves the processor's array behavior across supported Transformers versions.
- FunAudioChat accounts for the peak live padding, STFT, and log-Mel buffers. At the default byte budget, the standard 300-second checkpoint now allows up to three waveforms per prompt, subject to the configured item count.
- LLaVA-OneVision charges the effective sampled frame count. Gemma 4 resolves settings from its image processor call, and EmbeddingGemma2 uses the effective video geometry. Both retain the actual-byte check.
- The security guide and Rust README document the Rust frontend's 999-item default and how to configure the same 32-video item count as the Python frontend.

The new regressions failed on the previous PR head `1c7b97ea16`. Dynamic Nano accepted an over-budget request, Molmo2 returned 500 for incomplete resize options, and the tight-budget audio render accepted a waveform. LLaVA-OneVision and Gemma 4 rejected requests that fit. The stock EmbeddingGemma2 processor regression with a locally generated config and no weights also rejected a clip that fit its effective token setting (`1 failed, 1 warning in 5.58s` before and `1 passed, 1 warning in 9.07s` after).

### Sampling and CPU image budget review at `bbf9025f2a`

- EmbeddingGemma2 counts the effective sampled frames before allocating patches. It follows the processor's FPS and active overflow settings and avoids creating an extra sample-index array. The existing actual-byte check remains in place.
- Nano Nemotron VL reserves the largest full-resolution float32 source buffer on the CPU normalization path for both static and dynamic tiling. The budget accounts for the larger of the source cast and the concatenation copy at their respective stages. The resize operation and accepted pixel values are preserved.
- Qwen3-VL profiling and request preflight both follow the video processor instance's frame ceiling. CPU probes on Transformers 5.16.1 and 5.23.0 confirmed stock Hugging Face resizing uses the instance's `max_video_tokens`.

On the prior PR head `6343baa932`, the two EmbeddingGemma2 downsampling cases rejected in-budget clips (`2 failed, 2 passed, 19 deselected, 1 warning in 32.89s`). All four cases passed after the fix (`4 passed, 19 deselected, 1 warning in 29.42s`). The Qwen scoped-ceiling case generated two profiling frames where four were expected (`1 failed, 2 passed, 70 deselected, 1 warning in 2.07s`); the patched profiling selection passed (`3 passed, 70 deselected, 1 warning in 6.66s`). The old Nano code accepted below-limit-boundary inputs in both tiling modes and returned HTTP 200 where the CPU normalization render regression expected a budget error (`3 failed, 2 warnings in 7.07s`).

Changed-file and sign-off hooks passed. EmbeddingGemma2 was checked with a real Hugging Face processor and a local config. This follow-up was validated on CPU, including the render endpoints.

### Nano host accounting and Qwen profiling review at `ae14ec90a6`

Nano Nemotron VL charges actual host `uint8` tile bytes when normalization is deferred, plus resize working buffers or a concatenation copy as appropriate. The CPU normalization path retains the float32 source reservation. Dynamic device resize charges the aggregate original-resolution `uint8` buffers staged for upload. The security guide documents these host allocations. [Claude's Nano finding](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69098#discussion_r4668077888)

Qwen3-VL derives the profiling dummy frame count from the video processor's nominal per-frame ceiling. The shortest-edge floor still applies when resizing. On `bbf9025f2a`, a processed dummy produced five vision embeddings for a clip that used eight (`1 failed, 3 passed, 70 deselected, 1 warning in 3.02s` on Transformers 5.23.0). The patched dummy covers all eight (`4 passed, 70 deselected, 1 warning in 5.53s`). Four Nano regressions reproduced on `bbf9025f2a` (`4 failed, 2 warnings in 11.78s`). The patched set passed (`4 passed, 2 warnings in 10.78s`), including host render acceptance, resize temporary accounting, and raw staging rejection.


Changed-file and sign-off hooks passed. The device-resize test covers host staging. CV-CUDA execution and GPU profiling were outside this CPU validation.

### Waveform length and Nano test coverage at `90231e98e6`

FunAudioChat keeps a pre-decode count cap for the fixed processor buffers and estimates waveform copies from actual normalized sample counts before processor cache lookup. The regression accepts two short waveforms that the previous head rejected and rejects an over-budget short-plus-long pair after both clips are cached. The equivalent render test on `ae14ec90a6` returned HTTP 400 for the two short clips (`1 failed, 1 warning in 8.58s`). [FunAudioChat review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69098#discussion_r4668653543)

Collection with `-m core_model -k static_image_preprocessing_budget` selected zero cases on the previous head and four with this change. [Nano CI review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69098#discussion_r4668653559)

```text
11 passed, 40 deselected, 2 warnings in 16.61s
```

The FunAudioChat suite also passed on Transformers 5.16.1 (`10 passed, 1 warning in 27.82s`). Changed-file and sign-off hooks passed.

### Multimodal CI and main merge at `24511cdbab`

[Buildkite #105271](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/105271) showed that three existing Nemotron tensor-schema cases exceeded the request preprocessing budget. The fixture now uses the same profiling context as startup for its synthetic inputs. With a 1-byte budget and a local Nemotron configuration, the original fixture raised `VLLMValidationError` and the updated fixture produced batches of three images and three videos.

The merge preserves the patch-flat output introduced by #68808. The image budget now includes the peak memory used when packing those patches. Both new packing boundary cases failed with `DID NOT RAISE VLLMValidationError` before the packing cost was included.

On macOS arm64 CPU with Transformers 5.23.0:


commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Include the cause in HF processor error messages
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

When an HF processor rejects a multimodal input (for example, a 3×900 image on Qwen3-VL), the client gets a 400 that says `Failed to apply Qwen3VLProcessor on data=... with kwargs=...`, without the original exception message. `call_hf_processor` wraps the processor's exception in a new `ValueError`, and the API layer only sends the message of that outer `ValueError`. This change puts the original exception's type and message into the outer message.

## Claims

- A 3×900 image now gets `Failed to apply Qwen3VLProcessor (ValueError: absolute aspect ratio must be smaller than 200, got 300.0) on data=...`, and a one-frame video on Qwen3-VL gets `(ValueError: t:1 must be larger than temporal_factor:2)`. Before, neither reason showed up in the response or in the server log.
- Status code, exception type and the rest of the message are unchanged.

## Validation

A100-PCIE-40GB, torch 2.14.0+cu132, transformers 5.23.0. Main is `28fb1365a`, this PR is `edd0be110` (main + this change).

The new test `test_hf_processor_error_reason` sends a 3×900 image to the Qwen2.5-VL-3B server that `tests/entrypoints/multimodal/openai/responses/test_image.py` already starts.

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/entrypoints/multimodal/openai/responses/test_image.py -k test_hf_processor_error_reason
```

Main:

```
E       AssertionError: Regex pattern did not match.
E         Expected regex: 'aspect ratio must be smaller'
E         Actual message: "Error code: 400 - Failed to apply Qwen2_5_VLProcessor on data={'images': [<PIL.Image.Image image mode=RGB size=3x900>]} with kwargs={'do_normalize': False, 'do_rescale': False, 'return_tensors': 'pt'}"
================= 1 failed, 10 deselected in 68.22s (0:01:08) ==================
```

This PR:


One `/v1/chat/completions` message per request: the media item plus "Describe it.". The video is a single frame from `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc=size=320x240:rate=1:duration=1 -frames:v 1`.

Main:

```

Failed to apply Qwen3VLProcessor on data={'text': '<|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>', 'images': [<PIL.Image.Image image mode=RGB size=3x900>]} with kwargs={'text_kwargs': {'truncation': False}, 'images_kwargs': {'do_normalize': False, 'do_rescale': False}, 'videos_kwargs': {'do_normalize': False, 'do_rescale': False}, 'return_tensors': 'pt'}
```

I put the reason right after the processor name instead of at the end, because `data` can be long: a single 320×240 frame is already about 1.5 KB of array repr. Two things I left alone to keep this to one line. `data=` still echoes the whole input, and any exception from the processor still turns into a 400, including bugs on our side. If you'd like `data` bounded the way #54684 bounds validation errors, I can do that in a follow-up.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend][Perf] Default --renderer-num-workers to 4 for the async renderer
commits.pr_body:
By default tokenization is done by a single thread. In case of long prompts ~100k tokens this was limiting performance, engines were stalling. Then increase of renderer-num-workers to 4 helped to remove this bottleneck on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. So, this PR sets this setting by default for non-offline serving, for offline serving default keeps at 1.

## Testing Done

### e2e Qwen-Flash-Next (B200) **x1.75 perf** improvement

According to e2e Qwen-Flash-Next test renderer-num-workers set to 4 has the best perf

```
# server
vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 \
  --port 8000 \
  --data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --language-model-only \
  --stream-interval 100 \
  --renderer-num-workers 4

# benchmark
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 \
  --dataset-name random --random-prefix-len 99201 --random-input-len 0 \
  --random-output-len 1000 --random-range-ratio 0 --seed 0 --ignore-eos \
  --num-warmups 128 --max-concurrency 1024 --num-prompts 8192 --port 8000 \
  --ready-check-timeout-sec 3600 \
  --save-result --result-dir ab --result-filename result_rw4.json \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
```

| Metric | `--renderer-num-workers 1` | `--renderer-num-workers 4` | `--renderer-num-workers 16` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Output throughput, tok/s | 26,816 | **46,975** | 44,193 |
| Duration, s | 305.5 | 174.4 | 185.4 |
| Median TTFT | 21.4 s | **0.47 s** | 0.85 s |
| P99 TTFT | 32.8 s | 11.1 s | **6.1 s** |
| Median TPOT, ms | 14.3 | 19.8 | 20.3 |
| P99 TPOT, ms | 14.4 | 19.9 | 23.5 |
| Running requests (total), median | 404 | 996 | 1015 |
| Steady-state output, tok/s (median / p75) | 29.5k / 30.5k | 53.7k / 54.4k | 51.5k / 52.4k |

renderer-num-workers to 4 shows **x1.75 perf** improvement!

### e2e Qwen3.5-0.8B (RTX 5090)

Performance is the same in case of small model on consumer gpu.

```

vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B \

  --stream-interval 100 \

  --max-model-len 10240 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --renderer-num-workers 4

# benchmark
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B \
```

commits.pr_title: [Perf][ROCm][Attention] Use smaller tiles in the prefix_prefill kernel on RDNA (ROCM_ATTN prefill)
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On RDNA (`on_rdna()`), launch `prefix_prefill._fwd_kernel` with `BLOCK_M=64`, `BLOCK_N=32`, a 16-token KV tile and `num_unroll_cache=1`. `ROCM_ATTN` runs every prefill and chunked-prefill segment through this kernel. It is the default backend on gfx115x and the other RDNA parts except gfx1100/gfx1201, which prefer `TRITON_ATTN` since #60418 and use `ROCM_ATTN` only with an fp8_e5m2 KV cache or when selected explicitly. Other devices keep `128 / 64 / 32`, unroll 4. The gate follows the review on #63735; measured on gfx1151 and gfx1201, not on gfx1100.

Related: #58258 sets `num_warps=8` on gfx1100/gfx1201 for the same launch (compared below as `w8`); #63867 adds a `num_unroll_cache` variable at the same place (trivial rebase); #67445 would make `ROCM_RDNA_ATTN` the default on gfx115x.

## Claims

Serving on gfx1151, Qwen3-4B (`vllm bench serve`, PR vs main, > 1 = PR better):

| workload | median TTFT | mean TPOT | output throughput |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 in / 256 out, concurrency 32 | 1.14–1.16× | 1.03–1.04× | 1.04–1.05× |
| 8192 in / 128 out, concurrency 4 | 1.21–1.24× | 1.10–1.11× | 1.14–1.15× |

Kernel time, geomean over 84 bf16 shapes: gfx1151 2.62× (`w8` 1.99×), gfx1201 3.50× (`w8` 3.10×). Offline runs on five models (gfx1151) and two (gfx1201) agree; decode is unchanged. Full tables are in the details below.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_prefix_prefill.py --optional`: same result as main on gfx1151 (369 passed, 64 skipped) and gfx1201 (365 passed, 64 skipped, 4 reference OOMs on the 16 GB card on both sides).
- Max abs error vs an fp32 reference equals main's on every bf16, fp16 and sliding-window shape; fp8 KV within 1.14× of main's.
- GSM8K (5-shot, 1319 questions) moves −0.3 to +3.3 points across 7 model/GPU pairs, from the changed accumulation order.
- CI has no RDNA runner; the launch config on other devices is unchanged. pre-commit passes.

Raw `vllm bench serve` output for all 24 runs: [serve-raw-output.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35252985/serve-raw-output.txt). Kernel timing script: [pp-bench.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35252986/pp-bench.zip).

<details>
<summary>Serving: commands and all results</summary>

gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S). One server per run; runs ordered main, PR, PR, main; all 24 runs completed with 0 failed requests. The server logs `ROCM_ATTN`. Prefix caching is off so repeated runs with the same seed do not hit cached prompts.

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B --max-model-len 9216 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --no-enable-prefix-caching
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model Qwen/Qwen3-4B --dataset-name random --ignore-eos --seed 0 \
  --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency 32
vllm bench serve ... --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 128 --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 4
vllm bench serve ... --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 1
```

| model | workload | median TTFT | mean TPOT | output throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-4B | 1024 in / 256 out, concurrency 1 | 1.10–1.14× | 1.00× | 1.00× |
| | 1024 in / 256 out, concurrency 32 | 1.14–1.16× | 1.03–1.04× | 1.04–1.05× |
| | 8192 in / 128 out, concurrency 4 | 1.21–1.24× | 1.10–1.11× | 1.14–1.15× |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 ¹ | 1024 in / 256 out, concurrency 1 | 1.09× | 1.00× | 1.01× |
| | 1024 in / 256 out, concurrency 32 | 1.04–1.09× | 1.01× | 1.01–1.02× |
| | 8192 in / 128 out, concurrency 4 | 1.14–1.17× | 1.06–1.09× | 1.09–1.12× |

TTFT ratios are main / PR and throughput ratios are PR / main, so > 1 is better for the PR. At concurrency 1, decode steps do not reach this kernel, so TPOT is unchanged. At higher concurrency, prefill chunks share steps with running decodes, so a faster prefill also shortens TPOT.

¹ Both sides run with `VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS=RDNAHybridW4A16LinearKernel`. Without it, this checkpoint fails to load on gfx1151 on main in `rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py` ("zp row stride 640 must match scales 16"); see #63597.

|---|---|---|
| fp16 (28 shapes) | 1.21–7.39×, geomean 3.19× | 0.89–3.48×, geomean 2.21× |
| bf16 with fp8 KV cache (28 shapes) | 1.30–6.92×, geomean 2.88× | 1.24–3.28×, geomean 1.96× |
| bf16, sliding window 128 / 512 / 1024 (36 shapes) | 1.99–3.32×, geomean 2.86× | 1.61–3.24×, geomean 2.49× |

Timing: a HIP graph of up to 20 calls over rotating KV-cache copies (≥ 256 MiB working set). Each shape runs 15 rounds with the config order shuffled per round, and the per-shape median is reported. The timing script is attached (`pp-bench.zip`: `pp_bench.py`, which loads `pp_tunable_prefix_prefill.py`, a copy of main's `prefix_prefill.py` whose launch constants come from a module-level dict).

The config was chosen from a sweep of 73 launch configs (BLOCK_M ∈ {32, 64, 128}, BLOCK_N ∈ {16, 32, 64}, KV tile ∈ {16, 32}, warps ∈ {2, 4, 8}, unroll ∈ {1, 4}) on 20 shapes. It has the best geomean of any single config and reaches at least 0.75× of each shape's best config.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Tests and kernel correctness</summary>

**Tests.** `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_prefix_prefill.py --optional` gives the same result on main and on this PR:

</details>

<details>
<summary>Accuracy and host sync</summary>

**Accuracy.** The GSM8K prompts and answer parsing come from `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` (5-shot, all 1319 questions, temperature 0, `max_tokens` 256), run through `LLM(..., attention_backend="ROCM_ATTN", enable_prefix_caching=False)`. Repeat runs of the same variant produce identical text, on one machine and across machines.

| model | main | PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-4B | 0.8650 | 0.8620 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 | 0.8681 | 0.8787 |
| Qwen3-1.7B | 0.6679 | 0.6717 |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 | 0.6020 | 0.6353 |
| Qwen3.5-9B | 0.8650 | 0.8658 |
| Qwen3-4B, gfx1201 | 0.8597 | 0.8575 |
| Qwen3-1.7B, gfx1201 | 0.6581 | 0.6710 |

**Host sync.** `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` with this PR on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3.5-9B, covering throughput runs and 64 GSM8K questions: no error. The change only alters launch constants.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Notes</summary>

- **Scope:** the gate is `on_rdna()`, following the review on #63735. `get_rdna_version()` returns 3 for every gfx11 part, so it cannot single out gfx1151. Measured on gfx1151 and gfx1201; gfx1100 and the other RDNA parts are covered without being measured. The gate can be narrowed if preferred.
- **gfx1201 against #58258:** the kernel is faster with this config than with `num_warps=8` (geomean 3.50× vs 3.10×). End to end, the two give the same TTFT (offline table above), so either serves gfx1201 when it runs `ROCM_ATTN`. If both land, the second one needs to drop its gfx1201 branch.
- **Head size 64** gains least: 14 / 2 / 64 is 1.40–4.43× on gfx1151 and 0.97–3.57× on gfx1201, where one shape (1×512+2048) is 0.97×.
- **GSM8K differences:** they come from the changed accumulation order (BLOCK_N 64 → 32), which flips greedy decisions on a few questions. Qwen3-4B moves the other way from the other models.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Test environment</summary>

- GPU: Radeon 8060S (gfx1151, Strix Halo). Kernel and offline runs used 3 machines with the same image; serving used one. One test process per GPU, with no other workload on the machine.
- Container: `vllm/rocm10.1.0_ubuntu24.04_py3.12_pytorch_2.13.0_vllm_0.33.0_odinlink:gfx1151-v2`; torch 2.13.0+rocm10.1.0, Triton 3.8.0
- vLLM: main @ 8e45c458f vs this branch, with the Python sources mounted over the image; `_C` / `_rocm_C` built once from 8e45c458f (`PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx1151`) and shared by both. The PR branch is rebased onto ef687f617; `prefix_prefill.py` and `chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py` are unchanged between 8e45c458f and ef687f617
- gfx1201: Radeon RX 9070 XT (16 GB), one machine. Container with vLLM 0.34.0+rocm102, torch 2.14, Triton 3.9.0, whose `prefix_prefill.py` is identical to main @ 8e45c458f; main is the unmodified file and the PR is this branch's file mounted over it. With 16 GB, the Qwen3-4B and 8192-token runs set `enable_extensible_kv_cache=False`, otherwise the KV cache is sized for about 4 concurrent requests. Each process on this machine settles at one of two throughput levels for both variants (Qwen3-4B decode at batch 1: 51.7 or 69.7 tok/s, independent of the variant and the prompts), so ratios compare runs at the same level.

</details>

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Support DeepSeek V4 completion suffixes
commits.pr_body:
## Problem

The Rust frontend rejects every OpenAI Completions request with `suffix`, including requests for a gap between two pieces of text on DeepSeek V4. This addresses the completion-suffix item in #68784. Both #44229 and #9522 implement Python-side rendering.

## Solution

Use the selected renderer to prepare each text prompt before tokenization on `/v1/completions` and `/v1/completions/render`. The native DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 renderers use the same FIM markers as Python. Other renderers continue to reject suffixes. The request's `add_special_tokens` setting applies to the complete rendered prompt.

## Validation results

| Request | Main | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| V4, scalar prefix and nonempty suffix | HTTP 400 | The scripted engine receives the prefix and suffix between the three FIM markers. |
| V4.1, two text prompts and an empty suffix | HTTP 400 | The render route returns an independently framed token sequence for each prompt. |
| V4-Flash, live Rust render server | — | Every ID matches the Python renderer and checkpoint tokenizer for a code prefix and a two-prompt batch. |

The route regressions run with `cargo test --locked --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-server --lib completion_suffix_`. They also check the error field for unsupported models, token-ID prompts, incompatible options and empty inputs.

For a live check with `MODEL` set to DeepSeek-V4-Flash, start `vllm-rs render "$MODEL" --language-model-only --max-model-len 512` and POST `{"prompt":["一行"," x"],"suffix":"","add_special_tokens":false,"max_tokens":2}` to `/v1/completions/render`. The token IDs match Python's `[128801, 21988, 128800, 128802]` and `[128801, 1527, 128800, 128802]`.

## Limitations & follow-ups

The live check covers prompt preparation on the V4-Flash tokenizer. The V4.1 route uses a test tokenizer, and the generation route uses a scripted engine. The existing behavior for a scalar empty prompt without a suffix is tracked by #68098.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Parse Mistral v11+ tool calls
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Mistral tokenizers from v11 on render each assistant tool call as `[TOOL_CALLS]name[ARGS]` followed by its JSON arguments (Mistral Small 3.2 on tekken v11, Magistral and Ministral 3 on v13, Mistral Large 4 on v15). Python's `MistralParser` (`vllm/parser/mistral.py`, vllm-project/vllm#48947) picks the call format from the tokenizer, but the Rust frontend's `mistral` tool parser reads only the pre-v11 `[TOOL_CALLS] [{...}]` JSON array, so on every v11+ model the calls come back as content. The Mistral Large 4 model card's `--tool-call-parser mistral --reasoning-parser mistral` therefore loses every tool call on the Rust frontend. This PR makes the Rust `mistral` parser pick the format from the tokenizer, like Python, and parse the v11+ form.

For example, Mistral Large 4's chat template renders:

```text
[TOOL_CALLS]get_weather[ARGS]{"location": "Shanghai"}[TOOL_CALLS]add[ARGS]{"x": 2}</s>
```

## Claims

- `--tool-call-parser mistral` (and the `mistral-`/`mixtral-` auto patterns) parses `[TOOL_CALLS]name[ARGS]{...}`, repeated per call, when the tokenizer has an `[ARGS]` token; without one it keeps the existing pre-v11 JSON-array parser, renamed `MistralJsonArrayToolParser` and otherwise unchanged.
- Both markers are matched by token identity, so a model quoting the format with ordinary tokens stays text. The name is emitted at `[ARGS]`, and the arguments stream as raw JSON deltas.
- A v11 call ID (`name[CALL_ID]id[ARGS]{...}`, written by mistral-common's `InstructTokenizerV11`) becomes the call's `tool_call_id` instead of part of the function name.
- Output that ends inside a name or arguments is an incomplete tool call, as in the other parsers.
- A new `mistral_large4` case in the `vllm-chat` roundtrip harness covers Mistral Large 4 end to end with the model card's parsers.

## Validation

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`) on each commit, based on `ab1c06419c`:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # bans ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 40e5460e22 (parser): 2911 tests run: 2911 passed, 13 skipped
# d5bd5dd16b (roundtrip case): 2912 tests run: 2912 passed, 13 skipped
```

- New `vllm-parser` tests in `tool::mistral::tests`: calls after content; streaming at 1/2/3/7-character splits matching the complete parse, including a `}{` inside a string argument; the name emitted before its arguments; an ordinary-token `[TOOL_CALLS]` spelling staying text; a truncated call; a v11 `[CALL_ID]` call reported through `tool_call_id`; a pre-v11 tokenizer still parsing the JSON array.
- **Roundtrip case.** `roundtrip_mistral_large4` loads `mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B` (tekken v15) from the hub with `--tool-call-parser mistral --reasoning-parser mistral` and runs both fixtures: `reasoning_and_content`, and `tool_call_mix` (auto with content, required, named, plus the two schema variants answered with content). The output is rendered as `[THINK]...[/THINK]content[TOOL_CALLS]name[ARGS]{...}...</s>`, decoded one token per step, parsed, and re-rendered byte-identically. It also passes from an empty `HF_HOME`.
- **Red/green.** With `MistralToolParser::create` forced to the JSON-array parser, the four v11 behavior tests and the `tool_call_mix` roundtrip fixture fail, with the calls left in `content`.

## Details

- **Layering.** The call format is model-specific protocol recognition, so it lives in `vllm-parser`'s tool module as a parser type (`tool/mistral.rs`). Format selection sits in `ToolParser::create`, the one place that receives the tokenizer, so the chat crate's registration and auto patterns are untouched. The parser asks for special tokens to be preserved in decoding, since both markers are control tokens.
- **Call IDs.** When the tokenizer has `[CALL_ID]`, the name is held back until the ID is known. Python keeps the ID in the function name; v13+ encoders write no call IDs.
- **After a call's JSON object** only whitespace or the next `[TOOL_CALLS]` may follow; other text is a parse error, and the chat layer recovers the unparsed text as content.
- **Not ported from Python, on purpose:**
  - the `name{args}` fallback when `[ARGS]` is missing: tolerance for nonconforming output that no v11+ template renders;
  - dropping trailing text after a call's JSON (`raw_decode`, vllm-project/vllm#48975): here it is recovered as content instead of silently dropped;
  - Mistral-style 9-character call IDs on v11+: no v11+ template renders them, so Rust keeps its generic IDs;
  - dropping whitespace-only content before the calls: templates render content directly before `[TOOL_CALLS]`, so there is nothing to drop on conforming output;
  - a call grammar for `tool_choice` `required`/named on v11+ (Python gets it from mistral-common's Lark grammar): a possible follow-up; the schema variants of the roundtrip case exclude the calls, as for the other parsers without one.
- **Roundtrip prerequisites.** The case relies on Rust tokenizing with `tokenizer.json` when a repo ships both files (vllm-project/vllm#68911) and on the `mistral` reasoning parser (vllm-project/vllm#48013), both on `main`. Through `tekken.json`, Large 4 does not load, and a rendered `[THINK]` would be encoded as text.

**Not a duplicate.** A search of open PRs for Mistral tool calling in the Rust frontend found vllm-project/vllm#69060, which changes the pre-v11 JSON-array path (`[TOOL_CALLS]` as a special token); this PR leaves that parser's behavior unchanged apart from the rename, so the two overlap in `tool/json/mistral.rs` only textually. vllm-project/vllm#48320 and #68478 change Python's Mistral parser and grammars.

**AI assistance.** This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MoRIIO] Handle WRITE cancellation before submission
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix MoRIIO WRITE cancellation before the first submission so an aborted prefill request can release decode without waiting for a `write_done` that will never arrive. This builds on #59058. Related: #59382.

## Behavior

- If cancellation wins before any WRITE attempt, send `write_failed` to decode and release prefill through a single worker ACK. Use configured peer routing if decode has not allocated blocks yet.
- An empty WRITE plan does not count as submission. Once a WRITE may have been submitted, cancellation does not tell decode to reclaim blocks. Timeout and fencing are separate (#58962, #64154).
- This path is limited to matching TP sizes and PP=1.

## Validation

- **CPU:** 12 focused cases passed. Three focused regressions failed on the previous PR revision (`ba44da7`) and passed with this revision. Ruff and `git diff --check` passed.
- **GPU smoke:** Qwen3-32B with TP1 prefill and TP1 decode on two GPUs in one host, native MoRIIO RDMA loopback. Queue-time and post-allocation cancellation both issued zero WRITEs, with one ACK and one allocator release per side. Normal transfer and the post-submit control completed 64 WRITE submissions each.
- **Scope:** The GPU run used the candidate Python source with native libraries from the vLLM 0.34.0 / ROCm 10 image. I checked the raw events for the post-submit control because the original checker expected all WRITEs to return before a test barrier that intentionally held after the first return. This was a candidate-only smoke, not an unpatched GPU A/B, cross-host validation, or DMA fencing test.

<details>
<summary>Focused CPU tests</summary>

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_HOST_IP=127.0.0.1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/moriio/test_moriio_write_abort.py
```

</details>

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Accept `reasoning_content` and `join` in response templates
commits.pr_body:
Hi, Matt from Hugging Face here! I noticed the Python `hf` parser only accepts `thinking` fields in response templates, but the standard for chat templates is now `reasoning_content`. We didn't intentionally make this the standard, but it's clearly happened - virtually all modern chat templates now accept `reasoning_content`, and very few read `thinking`. The rust `hf` parser already accepts both.

This PR allows `reasoning_content` but keeps `thinking` as an alias. It also allows join on `reasoning_content` and `content` fields, which is needed to support some response templates, and updates the docs to match all of this.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Remove the phi4_mini_json tool parser
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend carries a `phi4_mini_json` tool parser (from vllm-project/vllm#44213) for Phi-4-mini's `functools[...]` tool-call format. This PR drops Rust frontend support for it: it is a low-value parser that would otherwise need its own follow-up work to stay at parity with Python, such as constraining `required` and named tool choice with a call grammar (vllm-project/vllm#68631). The Python frontend keeps serving `--tool-call-parser phi4_mini_json` unchanged, so deployments that need this parser stay on it.

## Claims

- With the Rust frontend (`VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`), `--tool-call-parser phi4_mini_json` now fails startup in config validation (`Config::validate` → `validate_parser_overrides`), before the engine handshake, with the usual ``tool parser `phi4_mini_json` is not registered (choose from: ...)`` error.
- No other parser changes behavior: the parser lived entirely in the parser crate and was registered by explicit name only, so the removal is a deletion.
- The Python frontend is unchanged.

## Validation

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`), on `73999a3a6e` based on `ab1c06419c`:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # bans ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast  # 2887 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `validate_parser_overrides_rejects_unknown_tool_parser` (`vllm-chat`): the snapshot of registered parser names no longer lists `phi4_mini_json`; it fails on the base and passes on the head.
- Startup check with a binary built from the same change: `vllm-rs serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser phi4_mini_json` exits 1 with `invalid OpenAI frontend configuration` caused by ``tool parser `phi4_mini_json` is not registered (choose from: ...)``; the same command with `--tool-call-parser hermes` passes config validation.
- No Python tests to enable or disable: `tests/tool_parsers/test_phi4mini_tool_parser.py` tests the Python parser and does not run against the Rust frontend.

## Details

- **Changes.** Delete `rust/src/parser/src/tool/json/phi4mini.rs` (parser and its unit tests) and its exports from `tool::json` and `tool`; drop the `phi4_mini_json` name and registration from the chat tool-parser factory, and the factory test `factory_new_registers_phi4_mini_json_by_name`; update the expected registered-parser list in `validate_parser_overrides_rejects_unknown_tool_parser`.
- **Layering.** The parser is registered only in the chat tool-parser factory, which `validate_parser_overrides` consults at startup, so removing the registration is enough for the frontend and the render server to refuse the name before using engine descriptors. The shared JSON tool-call core keeps every config feature the parser used (`,` delimiter: Mistral; multiple argument keys: InternLM2), so nothing becomes dead code. No docs, Buildkite step or e2e selection references the parser.
- **Deviation from Python** (intentional): the Rust frontend no longer accepts `--tool-call-parser phi4_mini_json`; the Python frontend does.

**Not a duplicate.** A search of open PRs for `phi4_mini_json` and the Phi-4-mini tool parser found vllm-project/vllm#68631, which changes the Rust parser this PR deletes (forced tool choice for `phi4_mini_json`), so this PR supersedes it; vllm-project/vllm#58072 and #48795 change the Python parser only.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Name the UTF-8 charset in SSE content types
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Python's streaming routes (chat completions, completions, Responses and `/inference/v1/generate`) return Starlette `StreamingResponse(media_type="text/event-stream")`, and Starlette appends `; charset=utf-8` to every `text/*` media type, so their header is `text/event-stream; charset=utf-8`. The Rust frontend's `sse_response` returns axum's `Sse`, whose header is a bare `text/event-stream`. HTTP clients that apply the `text/*` ISO-8859-1 default, such as Python `requests` (`response.text`, `iter_lines(decode_unicode=True)`), then decode the stream as ISO-8859-1 and garble every non-ASCII token. This PR names the charset on every Rust SSE response.

## Claims

- Every streaming response from the Rust frontend (chat completions, completions, Responses, generate) carries `Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8`, the same header as the Python frontend, with or without keep-alive.
- UTF-8 is the only encoding the SSE specification allows, so conforming SSE clients see no change; `requests`-style clients now decode non-ASCII tokens correctly.

## Validation

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`), on `6e8aa3644a` based on `ab1c06419c`:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # bans ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast  # 2903 tests run: 2903 passed, 13 skipped
```

- The existing `Content-Type` asserts in the streaming chat completions, completions and generate route tests now expect the charset, and the Responses streaming test (`routes::tests::responses`) gains the same assert.
- Red-green: with the header insert removed, those 4 asserts fail and the other streaming tests pass.
- With a UTF-8 SSE body such as `你好é`, `requests` decodes mojibake under the bare header and the original text under `charset=utf-8`.
- No Python test pins the charset (the Cohere SSE tests check `startswith("text/event-stream")`), so there is no Python test to run against the Rust frontend. No real-model run: the change is one response header.

## Details

- **Layering.** `sse_response` (`rust/src/server/src/utils.rs`) is the one SSE constructor in the server crate, and every streaming route builds its response through it, so the header is set once at the HTTP layer, on both keep-alive branches, rather than per route.
- **Deviations from Python.** None.

**Not a duplicate.** vllm-project/vllm#63926 carries the same header change bundled with a logprob token-string change that is a separate question; this PR takes only the header, so it can land on its own. A search of open PRs for the SSE content type and charset found no other PR on this path.

**AI assistance.** This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Keep each scheduler metric group in one place
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Regroups the Rust frontend's scheduler metrics so that each metric group keeps its payload, families, per-engine handles and recording in one place in `vllm-metrics`, with one module per KV connector. One small intended behavior change: NIXL and Mooncake transfer series are no longer exported as zeros on deployments without those connectors.

## Claims

- **Behavior change (commit 1):** `vllm:nixl_*` and `vllm:mooncake_*` transfer series appear when the connector first reports, instead of as zero-valued series on every engine of every deployment. Python builds a connector's metrics only when that connector is configured (`KVConnectorProm`), so this moves Rust toward Python.
- **Pure move (commit 2):** no exported metric changes. Series, `# HELP`/`# TYPE` lines and their order are byte-identical before and after.
- After this PR, adding a KV connector's metrics is one file in `scheduler/kv_connector/` plus one line each in the stats enum, `MultiConnectorStats`, `KvConnectorMetrics` and the dispatch.

## Validation

On head `16c534c446` (base `8e45c458f6`):

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check
cargo sort --workspace --check rust
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# Summary: 2885 tests run: 2885 passed, 13 skipped
```

Each commit was also validated on its own on the previous base `5cd63b656c` (fmt, `cargo sort --check`, `cargo deny check bans`, workspace clippy and nextest with `--all-features`: 2885 passed, 13 skipped on both). The six commits between the two bases touch only `managed-engine` and `cmd`.

- **Exposition diff.** A scratch harness (not committed) registers two engines with cache config info, records a full `SchedulerStats` (every core group, a `MultiConnector` payload with NIXL, Mooncake transfer, Mooncake store and UMBP children, then a bare NIXL payload) and a sleep state, and renders `/metrics` at startup and after recording.
  - Before and after commit 2, the sorted series and the `# HELP`/`# TYPE` order are byte-identical.
  - Splitting the core groups into one module each changed nothing either: the startup exposition with two engines resolved (sorted series and `# HELP`/`# TYPE` order) is byte-identical before and after the split.
  - Between base and commit 1, the only difference is the startup zero series of the 14 `vllm:nixl_*`/`vllm:mooncake_*` transfer families. The post-recording output is identical.
- **New test.** `kv_connector_series_appear_on_first_report` pins the behavior change. Its first assertion (no such series before a report) fails on the base.
- **Existing tests** move with their code, changed only for the handle API (`metrics.scheduler.resolve_handles(..)`, then `handles.kv_connector.record(..)` or `handles.state.record(..)`).

## Details

**Motivation.** A scheduler metric is spread over three files in two crates today. Take `vllm:nixl_xfer_time_seconds`:

- its wire field is in `NixlStats` (`engine-core-client/src/protocol/stats.rs`);
- its family and registration are in `SchedulerMetrics` (`vllm-metrics`' `scheduler.rs`);
- its per-engine handle, the handle's resolution and its recording are in `SchedulerStatsHandles`, `resolve_scheduler_stats_handles` and `record_nixl_stats` (`engine-core-client/src/metrics.rs`).

Each metric is written five times across those files, and adding a connector touches all of them.

**Layout.**

- **Core groups.** `scheduler/` has one module per group: `state`, `prefix_cache`, `spec_decode`, `perf` and `kv_cache_residency` (one per `SchedulerStats` part), and `engine_state` for the sleep state, LoRA info and cache config info, which do not come from `SchedulerStats`. `log_stats` holds the non-Prometheus text-log accumulators. Each module reads top to bottom: payload struct → families and registration → pre-resolved per-engine handles → recording, with its tests beside it. `scheduler/mod.rs` keeps only `SchedulerMetrics`, `SchedulerStatsHandles`, `resolve_handles` and the shared `EngineLabels`, and re-exports the group types. The core keeps pre-resolved handles because they are written on every step, and resolving them at startup exports zero series from startup, as Python's per-engine children do.
- **KV connectors.** `scheduler/kv_connector/` has one module per connector: `nixl`, `mooncake` (transfer), `mooncake_store`, `umbp` and `simple_cpu_offload`. Each module holds its payload decoder, its families and its `record`. Connector families are looked up at record time, so a connector's series exist only once it reports.
  - `kv_connector/mod.rs` holds the untagged `KvConnectorStats` (variant order is decode order, as documented), `MultiConnectorStats`, and the dispatch with the `MultiConnector` recursion.
  - `SchedulerMetrics` has one `kv_connector` field instead of 28 flat ones.
- **Payload placement.** The parts of `SchedulerStats` that only metrics read move into `vllm-metrics`, and `protocol::stats` re-exports them, so existing paths keep working. These are `PrefixCacheStats`, `SpecDecodingStats`, `PerfStats`, `CudagraphStats`, `KvCacheEvictionEvent`, `KvFetchReqsByStage` and every KV connector payload.
  - The `SchedulerStats` envelope stays in the protocol, because the client also routes on its request counts (`RequestRegistry::apply_scheduler_stats`).
  - `PrefillStats` (part of `EngineCoreOutput`) also stays.
- **Glue in `engine-core-client`.** It keeps only what needs its own types:
  - `SchedulerStatsRecorder` over the connected engines, including the cache config from the ready response. It hands each group's handles its part of the envelope.
  - The `SleepLevel` → sleep-state gauge mapping.

  `LoraInfoExporter` moves next to the `lora_info` family, since it needs no client types.
- **Field names.** Core group fields drop the prefix their group now carries, e.g. `scheduler.spec_decode.num_drafts`. `vllm-llm`'s text logger follows.
- **Exposition order** is unchanged, because groups register in the old order.

**Tradeoffs.**

- **Payloads sit inline in their group, not in a sibling `stats.rs`.** A sibling file would mirror Python's `vllm/v1/metrics/stats.py`, but it would bring back one of the jumps this PR removes.
- **Why the payloads moved into `vllm-metrics`.** They are part of the engine protocol's stats schema. Leaving them in the protocol would keep the payload and its recording split across the crate boundary, because `vllm-metrics` cannot see `engine-core-client`.
- **Remaining difference from Python.** When a connector is configured, Python pre-creates its per-engine children at startup, so those series show zeros before the first report. Rust's appear on the first report.

**Size.** The diff is +2775/−2427 across 22 files, almost all of it code moving between files. The net new lines are mostly the per-group structs and their `record` signatures.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR regroups these metrics. vllm-project/vllm#58563 (draft) adds a descriptor-driven path for connectors that Rust has no code for. That addresses a different problem and does not touch this layout.
