```bash
  tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_cutedsl_layout.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_unquantized_backend_selection.py
```

The backend-selection test covers the Hopper default and its fallbacks to Triton. `pre-commit` passes.

| with #9246 | 16 | output tokens/s | 2374 / 2422 | 2769 / 2756 | 1.15 |

## Details

- **Design**: a `FusedMoEExpertsModular` in the Standard activation format. The kernel call applies the router weights and combines the top-k routes, so weight-and-reduce is a no-op. `convert_to_unquantized_kernel_format` repacks w13 once at load into the kernel's 32-row up/gate interleave (same shape; gpt-oss's interleaved rows are unpacked first and intermediate padding is zeroed), and the intermediate size is padded to a multiple of 32.
- **Activation constants** come from the experts' `activation_config`, the configuration `apply_moe_activation` uses, so the kernel computes what the Triton path computes (for `swigluoai`, the fixed constants of `swigluoai_and_mul`).
- **Expert parallelism**: the kernel addresses a contiguous local shard from global top-k ids, so the backend supports TP and EP through the no-DP/EP and all-gather/reduce-scatter prepare/finalize, with the linear expert placement; `is_supported_config` refuses other placements under EP, so the Hopper default uses Triton there.
- **Not supported** (the backend reports the reason): activations other than bf16/fp16, expert biases, `gelu`, `swiglustep`, other `*_no_mul` activations, dispatching all2all backends, batch invariance, LoRA.
- **Hopper default**: with `--moe-backend auto`, Hopper tries this backend first and uses Triton for the unsupported cases above, FlashInfer without the kernel, or a non-linear expert placement under EP. The trade-off is prefill with little expert work per GPU: FlashInfer 0.7.3 spends about 200 us of host time per eager MoE call, so Qwen3-30B-A3B TP8 is on par offline and its concurrency-1 TTFT is 16% above Triton. flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#9246 removes most of that overhead (concurrency-1 TTFT about 7% above Triton) and is in the FlashInfer 0.7.5 release candidates; vLLM gets it once it pins a FlashInfer release that includes it.
- **Startup**: the CuTe-DSL kernels are compiled in each process; Qwen3-30B-A3B TP8 server startup took 271–340 s vs 265–300 s with Triton, and Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct TP8 with a warm compile cache took 360 s vs 361 s.
- **CI**: the MoE kernel job runs on L4, where the SM90 test skips, so this adds a small H100 job for it (about 5 minutes). The Qwen3-30B-A3B CuTe-DSL GSM8K config (CUDA graphs) joins the nightly H100 MoE integration list, and the H100 Triton config now sets `--moe-backend=triton` so it keeps covering Triton. The `test_moe_layer.py` helper now registers copies of the weights, since `process_weights_after_loading` may repack them in place.
- **Not a duplicate**: no open PR adds this kernel. #54742 changes the Hopper ordering of the FlashInfer CUTLASS backend and #49272 adds a DeepGEMM BF16 backend; both are different kernels.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this PR; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests, evaluations and benchmarks above.

Split out of #69259 (PR 0) with only the two sparse MLA indexer prefill bugfixes (@GirasoleY):

commits.pr_title: [Perf][GDN] Write only the used FlashInfer prefill checkpoint states
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

FlashInfer's GDN prefill with internal checkpoints (#60050) emits a state every N tokens of every sequence, where N is the gcd of the batch's checkpoint offsets. With a `--prefix-match-unit` of 128, a step mixing several prefills gets N = 128-256, so the kernel writes ~60-130 states and uses ~3. This PR passes FlashInfer 0.7.4's `checkpoint_state_indices` so only the used states are written.

## Claims

On Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, 1x B300, TP1:

- **GDN prefill kernel time per step drops by 34% or more** in a real server with mixed 16k-token prefill steps (torch profiler, 36 layers). The kernel cost drops to near the no-checkpoint lower bound.
- **Outputs are unchanged.** Microbenchmark outputs, final states and used checkpoints are bitwise equal to main, and GSM8K matches main.
- **Batches where every emitted state is used keep the existing call**, so FlashInfer's automatic CP route is still available.

| Per step, GDN prefill kernel | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Cached-prefix load (100k prompts, 5.9k fresh, c=16) | 15.80 ms | **10.48 ms** |
| `vllm bench serve`, random 4.2k-7.8k prompts, c=64 (2 servers) | 13.78 / 16.10 ms | **9.04 / 7.75 ms** |

The saving is ~2% of a ~300 ms prefill step. End-to-end throughput varies ±10% run to run in both arms on this setup (host-side stalls), so it can't resolve the change: 41.2k vs 41.9k tok/s, the mean of 6 runs per arm.

## Validation

All runs compare this PR (`2b97e2f516`) against main (`ad227db3ce`).

- **Unit tests:** `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_prefill_flashinfer.py` gives **75 passed, 2 skipped**. The skips are slots combined with forced CP, which FlashInfer doesn't support and the plan never produces.
  - The new plan and builder tests cover slots with and without unused states, and with and without spec-decode rows.
  - The export test writes into a NaN-filled buffer on both FlashInfer routes, so a missing or misplaced write fails.
- **Kernel microbenchmark** (CUPTI, cold L2). `dense` is main, `slots` is this PR, and `none` has no checkpoints:

  | query_lens | interval | states dense → slots | dense | slots | none |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | 3840+5920+5920 | 128 | 122 → 3 | 386.8 µs | 210.6 µs | 188.2 µs |
  | 1920+2080+5920+5920 | 256 | 61 → 3 | 438.4 µs | 255.7 µs | 255.8 µs |
  | 4000+5920+5920 | 128 | 123 → 3 | 386.4 µs | 211.8 µs | 188.2 µs |

- **GSM8K** (20-shot, chat, greedy, thinking off, c=64), flexible-extract: main scored 0.9492 / 0.9538 and this PR 0.9515 / 0.9507.
- **Resume:** 16 real-text prompts of 6k-43k tokens were sent cold in one batch, then sent again. All 16 warm requests hit exactly at their checkpoint in both arms.

Server flags: `--enable-prefix-caching --prefix-match-unit 128 --block-size 1920 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, with the Rust frontend and Rust `vllm bench serve` client.

I didn't use `vllm bench forward`: it disables prefix caching, so the checkpoint path never runs.

<details><summary>Microbenchmark script</summary>

```python
"""FlashInfer GDN prefill with internal checkpoints: dense vs slot-indexed writes.

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GDN shapes at TP1 (16 qk heads, 48 v heads, head dim 128).
Each case is one prefill step of several sequences whose checkpoint offsets
have a small gcd, so FlashInfer emits a state every 128-256 tokens while only
one per checkpointed sequence is used. Arms:
  dense: base behaviour, every emitted state written (buffer sized to them)
  slots: checkpoint_state_indices, only used states written
  none:  no checkpoints (lower bound)
Correctness: outputs, final states and the used checkpoints must be bitwise
equal between dense and slots.
"""

import pandas as pd
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time

from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.gdn.qwen_gdn_linear_attn import (
    fi_chunk_gated_delta_rule,
)
from vllm.v1.attention.backends.gdn_attn import plan_flashinfer_checkpoints

NUM_QK_HEADS, NUM_V_HEADS, HEAD_DIM = 16, 48, 128
NUM_GDN_LAYERS = 36
# (query_lens, offsets): 16k-token prefill steps mixing a partial chunk with
# full requests, each checkpointing at its last 128-aligned boundary.
CASES = [
    ([3840, 5920, 5920], [3712, 5888, 5888]),
    ([1920, 2080, 5920, 5920], [0, 1792, 5888, 5888]),
    ([4000, 5920, 5920], [3968, 5888, 5888]),
]

torch.manual_seed(0)
device = "cuda"
rows = []
for query_lens, offsets in CASES:
    n = sum(query_lens)
    q = F.normalize(torch.randn(1, n, NUM_QK_HEADS, HEAD_DIM, device=device), dim=-1)
    k = F.normalize(torch.randn(1, n, NUM_QK_HEADS, HEAD_DIM, device=device), dim=-1)
    q, k = q.bfloat16(), k.bfloat16()
    v = torch.randn(1, n, NUM_V_HEADS, HEAD_DIM, device=device).bfloat16()
    g = F.logsigmoid(torch.randn(1, n, NUM_V_HEADS, device=device)).exp()
    beta = torch.sigmoid(torch.randn(1, n, NUM_V_HEADS, device=device))
    init = 0.1 * torch.randn(len(query_lens), NUM_V_HEADS, HEAD_DIM, HEAD_DIM,
                             device=device)
    cu = torch.tensor([0, *torch.tensor(query_lens).cumsum(0).tolist()],
                      device=device, dtype=torch.int32)

    every_n, cu_starts, used_rows, slots = plan_flashinfer_checkpoints(
        offsets, query_lens
    )
    assert slots is not None
    num_emitted, num_used = cu_starts[-1], sum(1 for o in offsets if o)
    # Dense layout: state i of the emitted ones; the used ones are where slots != -1.
    dense_rows = [i for i, s in enumerate(slots) if s != -1]

    def run(arm):
        kwargs = {}
        buf = None
        if arm != "none":
            size = num_emitted if arm == "dense" else num_used
            buf = torch.empty(size, NUM_V_HEADS, HEAD_DIM, HEAD_DIM, device=device)
            kwargs = dict(
                state_checkpoints=buf,
                checkpoint_cu_starts=torch.tensor(cu_starts, device=device),
                checkpoint_every_n_tokens=every_n,
                checkpoint_state_indices=(
                    torch.tensor(slots, device=device) if arm == "slots" else None
                ),
            )
        fn = lambda: fi_chunk_gated_delta_rule(  # noqa: E731
            q=q, k=k, v=v, g=g, beta=beta, initial_state=init,
            output_final_state=True, cu_seqlens=cu,
            use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=False, use_cp=False, **kwargs,
        )
        out, final = fn()
        times = bench_gpu_time(fn, enable_cupti=True, cold_l2_cache=True,
                               dry_run_iters=5, repeat_iters=50)
        return out, final, buf, times

    results = {arm: run(arm) for arm in ("dense", "slots", "none")}
    d_out, d_fin, d_buf, _ = results["dense"]
    s_out, s_fin, s_buf, _ = results["slots"]
    assert torch.equal(d_out, s_out) and torch.equal(d_fin, s_fin)
    assert torch.equal(d_buf[dense_rows], s_buf), "used checkpoints differ"
    row = {"query_lens": "+".join(map(str, query_lens)), "interval": every_n,
           "states_dense": num_emitted, "states_slots": num_used}
    for arm, (*_, times) in results.items():
        row[f"{arm}_us"] = 1e3 * torch.tensor(times).median().item()
    rows.append(row)

df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
df["saved_us"] = df.dense_us - df.slots_us
print(f"{torch.cuda.get_device_name()}, FlashInfer GDN prefill, non-CP route")
print(df.to_string(index=False, float_format="%.1f"))
print(f"x {NUM_GDN_LAYERS} GDN layers, mean saving per step: "
      f"{NUM_GDN_LAYERS * df.saved_us.mean() / 1e3:.2f} ms")
```

</details>

## Details

- `plan_flashinfer_checkpoints` also returns `slots`, which maps each emitted state to its buffer row, or to -1 to skip it. `rows` and the exporter are unchanged.
- Slots rule out FlashInfer's CP route, so the plan returns them only when some emitted state would be unused.
- The plan still goes to the GPU in one H2D copy, with no new syncs. The profiling warmup compiles the slot kernel variant.
- A coarser interval doesn't help, because N has to divide every offset in the batch.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used.

## Overview `QWEN4_EXP_SM100_GEMM_PLANS` (`vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/low_latency_gemm.py`) has TP=4 (#59214) and TP=1 (#64482) shapes only. On B200, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next served at TP=2/TEP2 or TP=8/TEP8 therefore runs every BF16 decode projection through cuBLAS. In the FP8 checkpoint only the routed experts are FP8; GDN, QSA, shared-expert, router, HC and LM-head linears stay BF16. This PR adds B200-measured cuteDSL skinny-GEMM plans for the six TP=2 local shapes and the six TP=8 local shapes. It is table-only and SM100-only. It mirrors #64636 (SM80 TP=8). The TP=8 half was first opened as #69515 and is folded in here at the reviewer's request. ## Claims **TP=2 / TEP2** - **Kernels (B200, CUPTI, CUDA graph, cold L2), vs cuBLAS:** - GDN B/A 2.44–2.78× and shared-expert gate/up 1.54–2.00× at M=1–8. - GDN/QSA output 1.14–1.36× at M=1–4. - GDN QKVZ, merged QSA QKV/gate and LM head 1.15–1.19× at M=1–2. - **Forward step (TEP2, 2× B200, MTP3 drafter included):** −9.4% / −7.6% / −5.7% / −2.7% at 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 decode tokens; −5.7% / −3.0% at MTP3 concurrency 1 / 2. 16 tokens (no new entries) is unchanged. - **End to end (`vllm bench serve`, TEP2, no spec decode):** median TPOT −10.4% / −7.4% / −6.6% / −3.0% at concurrency 1 / 2 / 4 / 8, consistent across two alternating server starts per arm; re-tested on the rebased commit against latest main: −10.4% / −7.8% / −5.5% / −2.6%. - **Accuracy:** for every entry and seed, the max error vs an fp32 reference is identical to cuBLAS's. GSM8K is 0.968 / 0.967 (PR) vs 0.968 / 0.971 (main). - **Policy:** an entry is added only where the plan beats cuBLAS by ≥ 10% in the sweep, and never at M=16. At TP=4, M=16 entries regressed the full forward despite winning in isolation. **TP=8 / TEP8** - **Kernels (B200, CUPTI, CUDA graph, cold L2), vs cuBLAS:** GDN B/A 2.27–2.70× and shared-expert gate/up 1.99–2.70× at M=1–8; GDN QKVZ, GDN/QSA output, merged QSA QKV/gate and LM head 1.09–1.44× at M=1–4. - **Forward step, TEP8 (8× B200, MTP3 drafter included):** −9.0% / −9.6% / −7.7% / −2.8% at 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 decode tokens; −8.0% / −2.7% at MTP3 concurrency 1 / 2. 16 tokens (no new entries) is unchanged. Run-to-run variation ≤ 0.1%. - **End to end (`vllm bench serve`, TEP8, no spec decode):** median TPOT −8.9% / −10.3% / −8.5% / −3.2% at concurrency 1 / 2 / 4 / 8, consistent across two alternating server starts per arm. - **Accuracy:** max error vs an fp32 reference equals cuBLAS's for every entry. GSM8K is 0.968 / 0.967 (PR) vs 0.969 / 0.966 (main). - **Scope:** capability (10, 0) at TP=8 only. TP=4/TP=1 shapes and other GPUs are unchanged. M=16 and larger keep cuBLAS: the QKVZ/out/QSA/LM-head shapes lose to cuBLAS from M=8, and at TP=4 the M=16 entries regressed the full forward, so they are not added at TP=8. ## Validation Hardware: 8× NVIDIA B200 (driver 595.91.07), CUDA 13.2, torch 2.14.0+cu132, FlashInfer 0.7.4, Triton 3.8.0. **Commits.** TP=2 is `11a2d5f33e` on main `f08216eb63`. Next comes `f6e6b92372`, the merge of main (`504c9fc5aa`) by vllm-agent. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Config] Keep host-only renderer, timeout, and recovery fields out of compile cache key
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Six host-only config fields currently leak into `VllmConfig.compile_factors()` and invalidate compiled artifacts (and downstream keys built from `compile_factors()`, such as the FlashInfer tactic cache directory and startup plan):

- `ModelConfig.renderer_num_workers`
- `ModelConfig.allow_deprecated_quantization`
- `ParallelConfig.distributed_timeout_seconds`
- `ParallelConfig.cpu_distributed_timeout_seconds`
- `FaultToleranceConfig.engine_recovery_timeout_sec`
- `FaultToleranceConfig.request_failure_policy`

On stock vLLM (2x B300, TP2, `--max-model-len 4096`), adding a single host-only serving flag (`--renderer-num-workers 4`) to a warm restart invalidates the compile key and triggers a full recompile (+22.96 s on Qwen3-32B and +34.56 s on Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 including a FlashInfer tactic re-tune). With this PR, `--renderer-num-workers 4` reuses the exact AOT compile and FlashInfer tactic caches with zero new cache directories (**-21.22 s** on Qwen3-32B and **-33.50 s** on Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 vs stock).

This PR adds those fields to `ignored_factors` in `ModelConfig` and `ParallelConfig` and adds `FaultToleranceConfig.compile_factors() -> {}` (matching the existing `return {}` idiom in `DeviceConfig`, `LoadConfig`, `ObservabilityConfig`, `ProfilerConfig`, `StructuredOutputsConfig`, `KVTransferConfig`, and `ECTransferConfig`).

## Claims

- Changing any of the six host-only fields above no longer changes `hash_config(VllmConfig(...))` or `hash_config(ParallelConfig(...))`.
- Real graph- and collective-affecting fields stay unchanged and hashed, including `dtype`, `tensor_parallel_size`, `enable_fault_tolerance`, `async_scheduling_depth`, `dp_sync_interval`, and `disable_nccl_for_dp_synchronization`.
- `ParallelConfig.compile_factors()` is also used by DP worker compatibility validation (`vllm/v1/engine/core.py`, `vllm/v1/engine/utils.py`): relaxing mismatch checks on the four timeout/recovery-policy fields is deliberate because none of them changes collective communication patterns (`dp_sync_interval`, `disable_nccl_for_dp_synchronization`, and `enable_fault_tolerance` remain hashed).

## Validation

- Traced every reader of all six fields in `vllm/` to confirm none enters model construction, backend/kernel selection, traced forward execution, tensor shapes/dtypes, compilation passes, or CUDA graph capture.
- Added three unit tests in `tests/config/test_config_utils.py`:
  - `test_model_config_hash_ignores_renderer_and_quantization_validation`
  - `test_parallel_config_hash_ignores_timeouts_and_recovery_policy`
  - `test_scheduler_config_hash_includes_async_scheduling_depth`
- Verified locally on base `5cfdcabb24` (Python 3.12.16, `pytest` 9.2.0):
  - `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu pytest --noconftest tests/config/test_config_utils.py -q` → `33 passed in 10.61s` (`3 passed, 30 deselected in 2.52s` on the 3 new tests; running the same 3 tests against unmodified `5cfdcabb24` fails with `2 failed, 1 passed, 30 deselected in 2.87s`).
  - Verified individually on base `5cfdcabb24` that all six fields change the hash before this PR and leave it unchanged after.
- Verified `pre-commit` (`ruff check`, `ruff format`, `mypy` 3.11, `typos`, `check-test-tethering`, `check-forbidden-strings`, and config docstring validation) passes cleanly on all four modified files.
- **B300 TP2 end-to-end before/after (`vllm bench startup --serve-cmd`, `--max-model-len 4096`, cu135 image at `9c1d45c2` with the three config files patched):**
  - Each arm started from an isolated copy of the seed cache (`A`, `--renderer-num-workers 1`) and verified identical greedy token IDs (`8/8` match).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Guard Conch W4A16 preconditions and pad non-tile-multiple outputs
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`--linear-backend conch` dies at the first forward pass on `amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-INT4-W4A16`:

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-6 (Agent handle: 0x30a2bea0) on address 0x7e69a4600000. Reason: Unknown.
```

48 of the model's layers are fused `in_proj_ba` projections with `N=96`. Conch's W4A16 kernel loads the weight block and the per-group scales in 64-column tiles with no bounds mask, so the second tile covers columns 96-127: **128 B of packed weight and 64 B of scales per row past the end of the buffer**.

This PR handles those shapes in vLLM's Conch wrapper: a `K` the kernel cannot address is refused, and `N` is padded up to the kernel's tile width. All 48 layers then load and run - decode TPOT **-31.7% / -29.4% / -22.5%** vs the default Triton kernel at c=1/8/32 (8k-in / 1k-out). Selection is untouched: Triton stays the default, Conch stays opt-in, and conch
itself is not patched.

The change is shape arithmetic in the wrapper rather than anything platform-specific, so it should hold for any conch-enabled target; validated on `gfx950` (MI355X).

## Claims

* **Refuse the K side.** Every kernel implements `can_implement`, the hook vLLM calls to ask "can you run this layer?". `ConchLinearKernel.can_implement` now says no when the input dimension `K` is not a multiple of the kernel's 64-wide tile, or not a multiple of the quantization group size; channelwise layers (`group_size == -1`, one scale per output column) are checked as if the group size were `K`. None of this model's `K` values (5120, 6144, 17408) trip these, so the checks do not fire here - they stop another model from reaching the kernel with a `K` it mis-addresses.
* **Pad the N side.** Refusing works for K but not for N: under --linear-backend conch a refused N leaves the layer with no kernel at all. Instead the packed weights, their scales and their zero points are zero-extended along `N` to the kernel's tile width, and the extra output columns are dropped before the bias is added - `N=96` becomes 128 that way. The pad is taken from the unpacked launch-layout weight, so `N` must be a whole number of packing groups (8 for 4-bit); a partial group is refused at selection. This checkpoint has no `uint8b128` layers.
* **Refuse to serve stale weights after a reload.** The pad cache is derived state, and the layerwise reload path re-registers the pre-reload buffers while its captured metadata (recorded at model construction, before any pads exist) has no pads at all - so a reloaded padded layer would keep the old weights in its pads while the parameters get the new ones. Reprocessing a padded layer now raises with an actionable message. The check keys on a plain attribute rather than on the buffers, precisely because the reload deletes every registered tensor before it re-runs this method. Not covered: a reload that supplies weights already in kernel format (`is_checkpoint_format=False`), which skips weight processing entirely and so cannot be detected from inside the kernel; that combination is documented as unsupported.
* All 48 `N=96` layers load (`Using ConchLinearKernel for mixed-precision linear`), 0 memory faults.
* Decode TPOT **-31.7% / -29.4% / -22.5%** at 8k-in / 1k-out, c=1/8/32; our own A/B/B/A harness on short prompts gives **-38.1% / -37.7% / -36.6%** (method in the collapsible below). Prefill is slower - see the note under the bench table.
* Greedy 4/4 byte-identical between backends; gsm8k equal to the last reported digit.


## Validation

serving command, the two arms differ only by the flag:

```
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-INT4-W4A16 \
  --served-model-name qwen38-int4 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --seed 42 [--linear-backend conch]
```

bench serve command, c=1/8/32 (means, one run per cell):

```
vllm bench serve --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --model qwen38-int4 \
  --tokenizer amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-INT4-W4A16 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 0.0 --seed 42 \
  --num-prompts {8,16,32} --max-concurrency {1,8,32}
```

| c | TTFT ms triton -> conch | TPOT ms triton -> conch | output tok/s triton -> conch |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 908.4 -> 1240.8 (+36.6%) | 91.25 -> **62.30** (-31.7%) | 10.9 -> 15.8 (+45.1%) |
| 8 | 5253.6 -> 6698.1 (+27.5%) | 95.31 -> **67.25** (-29.4%) | 79.6 -> 108.4 (+36.1%) |
| 32 | 17926.5 -> 23007.2 (+28.3%) | 110.41 -> **85.57** (-22.5%) | 249.0 -> 295.1 (+18.5%) |

> Prefill is slower with Conch. Decode dominates an 8k/1k request, so end to end Conch is still ahead there (65.0 s vs 94.4 s at c=1, computed as TTFT + 1023 x TPOT), but prefill-heavy or short-completion workloads should stay on Triton - which is why Conch stays opt-in.

<details>
<summary>Decode TPOT, custom bench (A/B/B/A, two boots per arm)</summary>

Method: four server runs in A/B/B/A order (Triton, Conch, Conch, Triton), one backend per run, 128-in/256-out random prompts, 16/32/64 requests per cell at c=1/8/32, 256 generated tokens, p50 per boot; the cells are symmetric so the two boots of the same backend also bound run-to-run noise (p50 spread <= 0.03 ms for Triton, <= 0.44 ms for Conch). The same runs produced the greedy outputs used for the byte-identical check. Re-checked on the final revision: 46.98 / 47.78 / 49.53 ms, i.e. unchanged within noise.

| concurrency | 1 | 8 | 32 |
|---|---|---|---|
| triton | 75.91 | 76.55 | 78.18 |
| conch | 46.97 | 47.66 | 49.56 |
| delta | -38.1% | -37.7% | -36.6% |

</details>

`lm_eval`, gsm8k 25-shot, chat template, n=1319, 0 error rows:

```
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=qwen38-int4,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=10,max_length=8000,timeout=60000 \
  --gen_kwargs '{"max_tokens":4096,"until":[]}' --batch_size auto \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 25 --apply_chat_template
```

| arm | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| triton | 0.9704 +- 0.0047 | 0.9037 +- 0.0081 |
| conch | 0.9704 +- 0.0047 | 0.9037 +- 0.0081 |

Tests: `44 passed, 24 skipped` (gfx950) over the five quantization test files;
`pre-commit` passes on the two changed files. 

New coverage, all behavioural (real kernel, or the real reload entry points):

* `can_implement`: which shapes it refuses and why, the explicit-backend failure path, and `uint8b128` selection.
* Numerics against hand-computed dequantized references: symmetric `N=96` padding (bit-identical to a tile-aligned `N=64` layer), asymmetric zero-point padding (width and strides), and channelwise `group_size == -1`.
* Reload: driven through `record_metadata_for_reloading` and `initialize_layerwise_reload`, then a padded layer must refuse reprocessing.



## Details

The two loads that feed the tile in `conch/kernels/quantization/gemm.py` - the weight block and the per-group scales - are plain `tl.load`s with no bounds mask, unlike the masked loads and the masked output store next to them. With `N=96` the second 64-column tile reads columns 96-127, past the end of each row of packed weights and scales. If the following page is unmapped that faults (what we first saw); if it is mapped the read is silently out of bounds, and because the tail columns are masked at store time the results stayed correct in that case. A `K` that is not a multiple of the group size walks the scale buffer the same way, which is why the K side is refused rather than padded.

The fix is on our side because conch is pinned (`conch-triton-kernels==1.2.1`), its repository has been quiet since 2025-10-02, and the same unguarded code is in the 1.3 wheel. 

Notes:

* The pads live in three non-persistent buffers (each a tensor or `None`): out of `state_dict()`, moved by `Module.to()` / `Module.cpu()`, and kept at a stable address so CUDA graph replay reads them. That stable address is also why a reload cannot refresh them - see the guard above. Registered parameters keep their original shapes.
* The tile width is read from the kernel at first use rather than hard-coded. If that private helper disappears we fall back to conch 1.2.1's 64 x 64, which would silently under-pad if a future conch used wider tiles.
* A `uint8b128` layer whose `K` Conch cannot address is now unselectable (fails at selection with the reason) instead of being accepted and faulting at runtime.
* The reload gap is general, not conch-specific: registering a buffer does not make a layerwise reload refresh it (the reload restores the pre-reload captured allocation). It is tracked in the stable-runtime-tensor RFC (#57895) and being migrated kernel by kernel (#59000); until that lands, a padded layer refuses.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][CPU] DeepSeek-V4: return all layer types from the CPU tile scheduler
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On CPUs, DeepSeek-V4 raises `KeyError: 'c1a'` at the first decode step, since #56228. Every release from v0.30.0 to v0.33.0 is affected. The CPU `build_tile_scheduler` override omits the `c1a` and `c2a` keys that the shared sparse-SWA metadata builder reads. This PR returns them with the sentinel `None`, as the base builder does, and adds a regression test. Fixes #65364.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4 on CPU decodes again: a decode step through `DeepseekV4CPUSparseSWAMetadataBuilder.build()` no longer raises `KeyError: 'c1a'`.
- The new test fails on main with exactly that error and passes with this change.
- The CPU kernel CI step now also triggers on `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/cpu/` and `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_swa.py`, so a future change on either side runs the test.

## Validation

**Unit test** (`tests/kernels/test_deepseek_v4_cpu_kernels.py`), on main `66360a5cd0`:

```
# main (this PR's vllm/ changes reverted)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_deepseek_v4_cpu_kernels.py::test_cpu_swa_builder_decode_step_reads_every_layer_type -v
E       KeyError: 'c1a'
vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_swa.py:790: KeyError
FAILED ...::test_cpu_swa_builder_decode_step_reads_every_layer_type

# this PR
PASSED ...::test_cpu_swa_builder_decode_step_reads_every_layer_type
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_deepseek_v4_cpu_kernels.py -q
59 passed, 2 warnings in 42.57s
```

**End to end** on 2× AMD EPYC 9454 (2 NUMA nodes). DeepSeek-V4-Flash config with dummy weights: `load_format="dummy"`, `hf_overrides={"num_hidden_layers": 4, "num_nextn_predict_layers": 0, "quantization_config": None}`, `dtype=bfloat16`, `--enforce-eager`.

| Run | main `66360a5cd0` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| TP1, `CpuPlatform` | `KeyError: 'c1a'` at the first decode step | decodes (TP1, checked with the same setup on `6d01893483`) |
| TP1, `ZenCpuPlatform` | `KeyError: 'c1a'` at the first decode step (`sparse_swa.py:790`) | decodes |
| TP2, `ZenCpuPlatform` | – | decodes |

With dummy weights the generated text is meaningless; the check is that decoding runs.

**pre-commit** (full run) on the 3 changed files passes, including `ruff`, `mypy`, `typos`, the Buildkite step checks and `check-test-tethering`.

## Details

**Root cause.**
- #55355 added the CPU backend, whose `build_tile_scheduler` returns `None` for `swaonly`, `c4a` and `c128a`.
- A few hours later, #56228 (DeepSeek-V4.1) made `DeepseekSparseSWAMetadataBuilder.build()` also read `tile_sched[c1a]` and `tile_sched[c2a]` (`sparse_swa.py:790-791`), and extended the base `build_tile_scheduler` to all five types. The CPU override was not updated.
- GPUs use the base method, so only CPU fails.

**Why CI missed it.** The CPU kernel step runs `test_deepseek_v4_cpu_kernels.py`, but no existing test drives a decode step through the metadata builder. The step also did not trigger on the files involved. This PR fixes both.

**Alternative.** The override could return `super().build_tile_scheduler(0)`, which yields the base's all-`None` sentinel and would track future layer types automatically. I kept explicit keys to match the existing code; happy to switch if preferred.

**Not a duplicate.** No open issue or PR reports this (searched: DeepSeek-V4 CPU, `KeyError 'c1a'`, `build_tile_scheduler`).

**AI assistance was used** for the investigation, the change and test, and the validation runs. I reviewed every changed line and the results.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Let auto-rebase ignore per-step ci/step statuses
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Companion to vllm-project/ci-infra#928, which posts one informational GitHub status per CI step, named `ci/step: <step label>`. The auto-rebase rule requires `#check-failure = 0`, so a stale red step status would stop otherwise-eligible PRs from being rebased. This scopes that condition to every check except `ci/step: ...`. It must merge before ci-infra#928.

## Claims

- A PR with a green `buildkite/ci/pr` and a red `ci/step: ...` left over from an earlier build still gets auto-rebased.
- Any other failing check (`buildkite/ci/pr`, `pre-commit`, `DCO`, `pre-run-check`, docs, ...) still blocks the rebase, exactly as before.
- No other Mergify rule counts or matches checks by a pattern that `ci/step: ...` names reach; the pre-commit and DCO rules name their check exactly.

## Validation

`mergify config simulate -f .github/mergify.yml <PR>` (Mergify's own evaluation, read-only) at b658a83d, on two real PRs:

| PR | Failing checks | `-check-failure ~= ^(?!(@[^/]+/)?ci/step: )` | Rebase blocked? |
|---|---|---|---|
| #68524 (throwaway) | only two stale red `ci/step:` statuses; the latest build on the same commit is green | true | no |
| #69471 | `buildkite/ci/pr` red | false | yes, as on `main` |

On `main`, `#check-failure = 0` is false for #68524, which is the case this fixes.

- `mergify config validate`: valid.
- First draft used `^(?!ci/step: )`, and the simulation showed it still false on #68524. Probing showed why: for `~=`, Mergify matches each check both as `<name>` and as `@<app-slug>/<name>` (its app-qualified form), and the second doesn't start with `ci/step: `. Hence the optional `(@[^/]+/)?`.

## Details

- Kept the rule, narrowed the condition: `-check-failure ~= ^(?!(@[^/]+/)?ci/step: )` reads "no failing check whose name, with or without an app prefix, doesn't start with `ci/step: `". Turned down: listing the required checks by name (`check-success = buildkite/ci/pr` and so on), which would silently stop blocking on any check added later.
- Why a stale red can exist: GitHub keeps the newest status per name. If a later build of the same commit doesn't run that step, its old red stays even though the build passed.
- The merge gate is unchanged; `ci/step:` statuses are not required checks.

commits.pr_title: [CI][XPU] Enable batch invariance for OLMoE LoRA tests
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The XPU OLMoE LoRA DP2/EP test intermittently fails its case-sensitive SQL prefix check: `poll_source` becomes `Poll_Source`, and `count(*)` becomes `COUNT(*)`.

## Claims

Enable `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` only in the Intel OLMoE two-GPU CI job. CUDA, production defaults, and test assertions are unchanged.

## Validation

On Intel Arc Pro B70, using the original test at `75741803bd`:

- **Without BI:** failure reproduced on run **25** on XPU 6/7: **24 passed, 1 failed** (observed 4%).
- **With BI:** **100 runs without reproduction: 100 passed, 0 failed**. Four pairs ran 25 times each, including XPU 6/7; fresh engines, no retries.

On upstream main `66e8914fc9` with this change: the **entire test file passed**, `5 passed in 218.58s (0:03:38)`. Applicable pre-commit hooks passed.

<details>
<summary>Commands and raw results</summary>

Local environment: Python 3.12.3, Torch `2.15.0+xpu`, Transformers 5.22.2.

```bash
cd tests
export PYTHONPATH=.. VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1

# Original commit, without BI.
env -u VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=6,7 \
  /workspace/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  lora/test_olmoe_tp.py::test_olmoe_lora_dp2_ep

# Same original test, with BI; 25 runs per pair: 6/7, 8/9, 10/11, 12/13.
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=6,7 \
  /workspace/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  lora/test_olmoe_tp.py::test_olmoe_lora_dp2_ep

# Current main with the CI change applied.
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_TEST_DEVICE=xpu ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=6,7 \
  /workspace/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s lora/test_olmoe_tp.py
```

```text
E AssertionError: Output 2: 'SELECT Poll_Source FROM candidate GROUP BY Poll_Source ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1' vs 'SELECT poll_source FROM candidate GROUP BY poll_source ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1'
============================== 1 failed in 43.67s ==============================
============================== 1 passed in 49.93s ==============================
======================== 5 passed in 218.58s (0:03:38) =========================
```

Original CI failure:
https://buildkite.com/vllm/intel-ci/builds/19082#01a2076c-eb12-4739-903c-1fb51e585b3f
</details>

## Details

Without BI, even greedy decoding does not guarantee identical output across batch-dependent execution. Enable BI for these exact-output checks rather than weakening their assertions.

Duplicate checks found no matching open XPU CI fix. AI assistance was used.

commits.pr_title: [Startup] Keep Inductor and Dynamo imports off the non-compiled path
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Stop four vLLM-owned imports from loading Dynamo/Inductor on paths where the model is never `torch.compile`d (e.g. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MiniMax-M3-style specialized models running eager + CUDA graphs).

## Claims

- `kernel_warmup` no longer imports the MiniMax-M3 package for every CUDA model. Today it does, and that drags in the CuTe-DSL MSA kernels plus the Inductor fusion passes (`torch._inductor.pattern_matcher`, ~1.6 s of import on GB200) during warmup of unrelated models.
- MRV2's `metrics/logits.py` takes `libdevice` from `vllm.triton_utils` instead of `torch._inductor.runtime.triton_helpers` (same `triton.language.extra.libdevice` module).
- `InliningInstructionTranslator` (`compilation/decorators.py`) and the `InductorPass` wrappers (`config/compilation.py`) are imported only where they are used, so importing `vllm.config` or a `@support_torch_compile` model module no longer imports them.
- No behavior change.

## Validation

End-to-end, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (2 layers, dummy weights, TP1, GB200, FULL+PIECEWISE CUDA graphs, MRV2), with an import tracer recording which vLLM frames import `torch._dynamo*`/`torch._inductor*` or call `torch.compile`:

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Generation (4 × 8 tokens) | OK | OK |
| `vllm.models.minimax_m3` loaded | yes (from `kernel_warmup`) | no |
| `torch._inductor.pattern_matcher` imported from `kernel_warmup` → MiniMax-M3 → fusion passes | yes | no |
| `torch._inductor.runtime.triton_helpers` imported from `metrics/logits.py` | yes | no |
| `torch._dynamo.symbolic_convert` imported from `compilation/decorators.py` | yes | no |
| `torch._inductor.custom_graph_pass` imported from `config/compilation.py` | yes | no |

Remaining heavy-Inductor sources on this path are module-level `@torch.compile` decorators (`deep_gemm.py`, `fused_moe/utils.py`, `grouped_topk_router.py`, `vocab_parallel_embedding.py`, `philox.py`), which this PR intentionally does not touch. Dynamo itself is still imported by transformers (`masking_utils` via `tokenization_auto`) and torchvision, outside vLLM's control.

```bash
pre-commit run --files <changed files>   # all pass, incl. mypy
pytest tests/utils_/test_gpu_sync_debug.py tests/utils_/test_deep_gemm_utils.py \
       tests/kernels/moe/test_grouped_topk.py tests/watermarking/test_prf.py \
       tests/watermarking/test_goldens.py tests/quantization/test_online.py
```

No new test: the warmup gate is a one-line `sys.modules` check, and exercising `kernel_warmup` needs a heavily faked worker; the e2e trace above is the evidence.

## Details

- **MiniMax gate**: `minimax_m3_msa_warmup` already returns early when the model has no `MiniMaxM3SparseAttention`, but importing it was the cost. Every MiniMax-M3 architecture in the registry (including its MTP/DSpark drafters) lives under `vllm.models.minimax_m3`, so `"vllm.models.minimax_m3" in sys.modules` is exactly "this model could have MSA layers".
- **libdevice**: the module-level name `libdevice` is kept so platform plugins that rebind `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.metrics.logits.libdevice` (vllm-ascend does, to the CANN libdevice) keep working.
- `torch._inductor.config` is still imported in `CompilationConfig.__post_init__` for the `combo_kernels` defaults. It costs nothing beyond the Dynamo import that transformers already forces, and gating it would change compile-config hashing, so it is left as is.
- Plugins: checked vllm-ascend and vllm-torchtpu (including torchtpu's `sitecustomize.py`) for references to `InliningInstructionTranslator`, `InductorPass`/`CallableInductorPass`, `vllm.compilation.passes`, `kernel_warmup`, the MiniMax warmup, and `metrics.logits`/`get_num_nans`: the only one is vllm-ascend rebinding `logits.libdevice`, which still works. vllm-torchtpu patches `decorators._try_load_aot_compiled_fn` in tests (untouched), and code that reads `torch._dynamo.*` without importing it still works since torch lazily imports `torch._dynamo` on attribute access (torch 2.13, torchtpu's pin, and 2.14). The `kernel_warmup` gate sits under `current_platform.is_cuda()`, and `libdevice` is only read inside the `@triton.jit` body, so neither path runs on TPU/NPU. Not run on TPU hardware (vllm-torchtpu needs x86_64 `torch_tpu` wheels).
- Not a duplicate: open PRs in this area defer module-level `torch.compile` decorators or touch `env_override.py`; this PR touches neither.

commits.pr_title: [EPD] Support metadata-only images and videos for HY4 and HY4 Flash
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Enable metadata-only image and video forwarding in the Python EPD proxy for HY4 and HY4 Flash. Both models use the same multimodal processor and vision projector.

Related: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52409

## Claims

- The proxy forwards vision grids and video timestamps. PD reconstructs the visual placeholders and M-RoPE positions, and ECMooncake supplies the embeddings.
- On Hy4-flash-FP8, metadata-only reduced p50 TTFT by 15.9% for an image and 19.2% for a short video in the tested EPD workload. All 40 measured pairs produced identical greedy token IDs.
- On Hy4-FP8 over RDMA, metadata-only reduced p50 TTFT by 8.8% for an image and 16.9% for a short video. All 40 measured pairs produced identical greedy token IDs and the proxy-to-PD body shrank by more than 99%; over TCP the same comparison measured at parity.

## Validation

### Hy4-flash-FP8

Hy4-flash-FP8 real weights on one H200 node with Encoder TP1, PD TP4, ECMooncake TCP, the Python frontend, and eager mode. The baseline used the same workers with the proxy's `--no-rewrite` flag. Each workload used 3 warm-up pairs followed by 20 randomized-order pairs with fresh media UUIDs and 16 greedy output tokens.

| Input | TTFT p50, raw → metadata | TTFT p90, raw → metadata | Proxy → PD body p50, raw → metadata |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Image, 760 × 1024 | 363.4 → 305.7 ms | 373.9 → 315.1 ms | 458,532.5 → 621.5 B |
| Video, 448 × 448, 8 frames at 4 fps | 394.2 → 318.6 ms | 433.3 → 337.5 ms | 73,211.5 → 699.5 B |

Five Flash E2E cases matched prompt token IDs and all 16 generated token IDs. The proxy logs showed metadata rewrites. Both checkpoint processors matched raw-media prompt tokens and placeholder ranges on the same five scenarios, including explicit video timing.

### Hy4-FP8

Real weights with Encoder TP1 and PD TP8 on separate H200 nodes, using ECMooncake RDMA (UCX over the nodes' InfiniBand NICs) and the same raw-media baseline, requests, and sampling protocol as Flash. Five E2E cases matched the prompt and all 16 output tokens. All 40 benchmark pairs matched the output token IDs; 19 of 20 pairs per input ran faster in metadata mode. The PD receive pool ran at 2 GiB; the initial 128 MiB pool filled during the first benchmark attempt. Over TCP the same comparison measured at parity (image 451.1 → 450.5 ms, video 473.5 → 463.3 ms).

| Input | TTFT p50, raw → metadata | TTFT p90, raw → metadata | Proxy → PD body p50, raw → metadata |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Image, 760 × 1024 | 541.8 → 494.1 ms | 554.7 → 517.1 ms | 458,526.5 → 615.5 B |
| Video, 448 × 448, 8 frames at 4 fps | 479.0 → 397.9 ms | 591.6 → 511.0 ms | 73,205.5 → 693.5 B |

<details>
<summary>Hy4-flash-FP8 CLI (Encoder TP1, PD TP4)</summary>

Start the Encoder and PD from a CUDA-enabled checkout with Mooncake installed.

```bash
vllm serve /models/Hy4-flash-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 19180 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.25 \
  --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 4 \
  --enforce-eager --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-request-id-headers \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":2,"video":2}' --trust-request-mm-kwargs --generation-config vllm \
  --ec-transfer-config '{"ec_connector":"ECMooncakeConnector","ec_role":"ec_producer","ec_buffer_size":134217728,"ec_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"tcp"}}'

vllm serve /models/Hy4-flash-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 19181 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.87 \
  --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 4 \
  --enforce-eager --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-request-id-headers \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":2,"video":2}' --trust-request-mm-kwargs --generation-config vllm \
  --ec-transfer-config '{"ec_connector":"ECMooncakeConnector","ec_role":"ec_consumer","ec_port":19190,"ec_buffer_size":134217728,"ec_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"tcp"}}'
```

Run the two serve commands in separate shells. Once both workers are healthy, start the stock proxy in rewrite and baseline modes.

```bash
proxy=examples/disaggregated/disaggregated_encoder/disagg_epd_proxy.py
route=(--host 127.0.0.1 --encode-servers-urls http://127.0.0.1:19180
  --decode-servers-urls http://127.0.0.1:19181 --prefill-servers-urls disable
  --ec-consumer-zmq-addrs tcp://127.0.0.1:19190)
.venv/bin/python "$proxy" "${route[@]}" --port 19184 &
.venv/bin/python "$proxy" "${route[@]}" --port 19185 --no-rewrite &
```

Send the same media and prompt to both ports. Compare prompt and generated token IDs with `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=16`, and `return_token_ids=true`. For the benchmark, stream the responses and measure elapsed time to the first output token. The local driver `bench-flash.py` interleaves requests to ports 19184 and 19185 and records the proxy-to-PD JSON body size from a log line added to the measurement copy of the proxy.

```bash
.venv/bin/python bench-flash.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_hy_v4.py
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hy4-FP8 CLI (Encoder TP1, PD TP8)</summary>

Run Encoder and PD on separate H200 nodes with InfiniBand between them. Replace `ENCODER_IP` and `PD_IP` with the addresses reachable between the two workers, and set `UCX_NET_DEVICES` to the compute NICs of the machine.

```bash
export UCX_TLS=all UCX_CUDA_COPY_DMABUF=no
export UCX_NET_DEVICES=mlx5_0:1,mlx5_1:1,mlx5_2:1,mlx5_5:1,mlx5_6:1,mlx5_7:1,mlx5_8:1,mlx5_10:1

vllm serve /models/Hy4-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --host ENCODER_IP --port 19180 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.25 \
  --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 4 \
  --enforce-eager --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-request-id-headers \
  --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE --generation-config vllm \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":2,"video":2}' --trust-request-mm-kwargs \
  --ec-transfer-config '{"ec_connector":"ECMooncakeConnector","ec_role":"ec_producer","ec_buffer_size":134217728,"ec_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"rdma"}}'

vllm serve /models/Hy4-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 19181 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --load-format fastsafetensors \
  --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 4 \
  --enforce-eager --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-request-id-headers \
  --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE --generation-config vllm \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":2,"video":2}' --trust-request-mm-kwargs \
  --ec-transfer-config '{"ec_connector":"ECMooncakeConnector","ec_role":"ec_consumer","ec_ip":"PD_IP","ec_port":19190,"ec_buffer_size":2147483648,"ec_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"rdma"}}'
```

Start the same two proxy modes on the PD node as in the Flash run. Point both proxies at `http://ENCODER_IP:19180` and set `--ec-consumer-zmq-addrs tcp://PD_IP:19190`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python bench-hy4.py
```

</details>

Unit tests on `5fe37febb3`: `10 passed, 1 warning in 0.15s`. The projector test covers `None` and `rmsnorm_mlp_adapter`.

## Details

The shared HY4 parser declares the metadata fields and checks grid validity, context bounds, and video timestamp counts before expanding placeholders. The vision projector emits contiguous tensors for Mooncake. Flash skips the text weight audit in encoder-only mode, where only the vision tower is loaded. The text audit remains active on PD.

Duplicate-work check found Rust frontend work in #68714 and #68274. This PR adds model-side support in the Python HY4 processor and vision stack.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Serve Nemotron VL and Omni multimodal inputs
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The Rust frontend serves image and video inputs for three Nemotron checkpoints: Nano 12B V2 VL, 3 Nano Omni and 3.5 Super VL. It bumps `llm-multimodal` to current `smg-project/smg` main, which holds the Nemotron specs of smg-project/smg#7137, and adapts the frontend to them.

## Claims

- The Rust frontend serves one or several images, one or several videos, and images mixed with videos for the three checkpoints. It sends the tensors that `nano_nemotron_vl.py` reads.
- Prompt tokens equal the Python frontend's on every request that Python accepts, for Nano Omni and Nano V2 VL. For Super VL they are equal for images. Super VL video frames follow the checkpoint's `preprocessor_config.json`, as Python does with #68776.
- A checkpoint whose `config.json` holds a bare `Infinity` (Nano V2 VL) loads in the Rust frontend.
- Other models keep their `is_embed` masks and tensors.

## Validation

Branch head a19eab84e.

**Unit tests and lints** (in `rust/`):

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                   ok
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings        ok
cargo test -p vllm-chat --lib      test result: ok. 539 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p vllm-server --lib    test result: ok. 722 passed; 0 failed
```

`cargo test -p vllm-text --lib` has one failure, `lower_text_request_uses_real_qwen_generation_defaults`. It fails the same way on `main` on my machine.

New tests:

- `nemotron_images_of_different_sizes_are_separate_items`
- `nemotron_video_carries_frame_indices_and_embeds_the_whole_replacement` (RGB clip and image-frame clip)
- `rewrites_one_rendered_marker_per_media_item`
- `expand_prompt_tokens_leaves_is_embed_unset_for_an_all_feature_replacement`
- `lenient_json_reads_bare_constants_outside_strings_as_null`

**End to end**, x86-64 with H100 GPUs. The branch applied on the `nightly-9c1d45c21` image, one server per frontend, 23 requests per model, greedy decoding.

```bash
# Python frontend, with the CPU normalization that the Rust frontend also uses
vllm serve $MODEL --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 32768 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' \
  --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 --no-mm-device-do-normalize
# Rust frontend
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 VLLM_RUST_FRONTEND_PATH=$VLLM_RS vllm serve $MODEL --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 32768 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'
```

| Model | Python accepts | Same prompt tokens | Same text |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nano Omni | 19 of 23 | 19 of 19 | 19 of 19 |
| Nano V2 VL | 22 of 23 | 22 of 22 | 17 of 22 |
| Super VL | 22 of 23 | 11 of 22 | 10 of 22 |

- The Rust frontend answers all 23 requests for each model.
- Python refuses the 4K video because of `VLLM_MAX_MEDIA_REQUEST_DECODE_BYTES`. For Nano Omni, Python's processor also fails on the three requests that hold videos of different frame sizes.
- Super VL: the 11 requests with equal tokens are all the image requests and the square video. The other video requests differ because Python, without #68776, resizes Super VL frames to 512x512.
- Greedy text is not stable across restarts of one server, so the text column is limited by noise. Over three runs of this sweep, prompt tokens were the same each time. The matching texts went from 15 to 19 of 19 for Nano Omni and from 17 to 22 of 22 for Nano V2 VL. Between two runs, the Python Nano Omni server alone changed 4 of 19 texts.
- A 200 answer for two clips of different frame sizes does not show correct embeddings. See the first limit below.

**Accuracy and performance** are in smg-project/smg#7137. They were measured through an earlier revision of this integration with the same crate code. OCRBench v2 and VideoMME short differ by at most 0.13 and 0.67 points between the frontends.

No CI job has these checkpoints, so the end-to-end checks ran outside CI.

## Details

**Frontend changes**

- `lookup_spec` reads `ModelRegistry::for_format(EncoderInputFormat::Reference)`. That registry holds the specs whose tensors vLLM reads.
- Images: the processor can return one batch per image, because dynamic-resolution images do not share a shape. Each batch becomes its own items, with hashes and uuids in request order.
- Video: the processor gets the decoder's source frame indices, which the Nemotron timestamps need. When the decoder returns a clip as image frames (its last fallback), the frontend retries through the RGB entry point, because the image-frame entry point takes no indices.
- Marker text: the Nemotron template writes `<video>` for a video, and the spec expands a placeholder token. The frontend rewrites the text to that token before it tokenizes, once per video in the request. It cannot match `<video>` as a multi-token marker, because its tokens depend on the text around it.
- `is_embed`: a replacement that the spec declares as all features gets no mask, as `PromptUpdateDetails.from_seq` in Python. Only the Nemotron video replacement is such a case. The embed-token rule stays for everything else.
- JSON: for `config.json` only, `from_lenient_json` reads bare `NaN`, `Infinity` and `-Infinity` outside strings as `null`. Python reads them as floats. `serde_json` has no such numbers, and no Rust code reads those fields.

**Limits**

- Clips of different frame sizes in one encoder batch. Nano Omni and Super VL keep each clip's aspect ratio. The engine pads video items of different frame sizes to one size (`MultiModalFlatField`), and the model reads one frame size per batch. `requires_sequential_video_encoding` on the model is not read anywhere. From the code, such a batch gets wrong embeddings. No run confirmed this. It also applies to the Python frontend when concurrent requests hold such clips. It needs an engine fix, which is not in this PR.
- Audio for Nano Omni needs the Python frontend. The Rust frontend answers an audio request with an unsupported-modality error.
- A pre-tokenized prompt (gRPC `token_ids`, `/inference/v1/generate`) must hold the placeholder token for a video, not tokenized `<video>` text.
- The Rust frontend has no decoded-media size cap like `VLLM_MAX_MEDIA_REQUEST_DECODE_BYTES`. This PR does not change that.
- A dynamic-resolution image gets a smaller grid when the context is almost full, as on `main` for Nano Omni. The cache key of the image does not include the grid.

**Other effects of the bump**

- The crate now has `inkling2` and `nemotron_transcribe` specs. The local `inkling2` spec stays first, because the two differ in the placeholder they expand. A config that names only the Inkling2 architecture, with no known `model_type`, reaches the crate's spec.
- The reference registry has no MuseSpark spec. The local MuseSpark spec serves that model.
- The bump takes every other crate change between the two revisions.
- The crate's API changes are taken as they are: shared media URLs, two base64 media parts, and the text of one media error.

commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCm] Spawn the GPU memory wait worker
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On ROCm, run the `tests/utils.py` GPU memory-wait worker with `spawn` instead of `fork`. A forked worker cannot use HIP if the parent pytest process already initialized HIP outside torch, and `VllmRunner` then fails with `hipErrorInvalidValue` before it builds an `LLM`.

This fixes the AMD `(MI300) V1 Attention Shard 4/6` failure in `v1/attention/test_encoder_only_attention_hooks_e2e.py` (added in #67798). It fails on every PR whose shard runs that file after `test_encoder_only_attention_hooks.py`, for example builds [104918](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/104918) (#63402), [105026](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/105026) (#69056), [105040](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/105040) (#68596) and [105042](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/105042) (#63002). It also covers the default-`fork` case of the failure that #68068 fixed for explicit `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn`.

## Claims

- On ROCm, the GPU memory wait no longer depends on which tests ran earlier in the same pytest process.
- The pytest process still stays HIP-free, so vLLM keeps forking its engine processes (the goal of #67821).
- CUDA, XPU, the in-process path for already-initialized HIP and the explicit-`spawn` path from #68068 are unchanged.
- No measurable slowdown: the e2e test alone took 41.2 s with `spawn` and 40.2 s with `fork` (one run each).

## Validation

Image: `rocm/vllm-dev:build-01a20715-61bc-42fd-8075-80aa68baf952`, the AMD test image of CI build 105040 (`178b29a`, the #68596 head on main `eff4de9`). Its `tests/utils.py` is byte-identical to this PR's base, `b26e084`, before the change. Hardware: 1x MI355X per run (`HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<n>`), torch `2.13.0+rocm10.0.0`. The "with fix" runs apply this diff on top of the image.

**Same shard as the failing CI job, 18 files in CI order**, run 10x with the fix and 1x without:

```bash
cd /vllm-workspace/tests
pytest -v -s v1/attention/test_aiter_mla_uniform_mtp_qo_len.py v1/attention/test_attention_backends_selection.py v1/attention/test_cpu_mla_backend.py v1/attention/test_cuda_backend_probe_errors.py v1/attention/test_encoder_only_attention_hooks.py v1/attention/test_encoder_only_attention_hooks_e2e.py v1/attention/test_fa4_dense_warmup.py v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_workspace.py v1/attention/test_kv_head_stride_canonicalization.py v1/attention/test_mamba_align_block_table.py v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_context_nvfp4.py v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr_numerics.py v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_verify_gfx942.py v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py v1/attention/test_rocm_gqa_verify.py v1/attention/test_triton_attn_metadata_builder.py v1/attention/test_triton_attn_segments.py v1/attention/test_xpu_mla_sparse_backend.py
```

| | Runs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Without fix | 1 | `2 failed, 1037 passed, 29 skipped`: both `test_model_owned_backend_on_half_the_layers[TRITON_ATTN-*]`, `hipErrorInvalidValue` |
| With fix | 10 | `1039 passed, 29 skipped` in every run, 15:49 to 19:19 |

One more run with the fix failed one case for an unrelated reason: another user's job took about 36 GiB on that GPU after the memory wait had passed (`ValueError: Free memory on device cuda:0 (251.73/287.98 GiB) on startup is less than desired GPU memory utilization`). That run is not counted. Its replacement ran on an idle GPU with memory monitoring and passed.

<details>
<summary>Raw output</summary>

Without fix:
```text
FAILED v1/attention/test_encoder_only_attention_hooks_e2e.py::test_model_owned_backend_on_half_the_layers[TRITON_ATTN-True]
FAILED v1/attention/test_encoder_only_attention_hooks_e2e.py::test_model_owned_backend_on_half_the_layers[TRITON_ATTN-False]

```

With fix, the 10 counted runs:
```text
========== 1039 passed, 29 skipped, 349 warnings in 949.34s (0:15:49) ==========
========== 1039 passed, 29 skipped, 349 warnings in 964.20s (0:16:04) ==========
========= 1039 passed, 29 skipped, 349 warnings in 1033.93s (0:17:13) ==========
========= 1039 passed, 29 skipped, 349 warnings in 1105.88s (0:18:25) ==========

```
</details>

**Minimal reproducer** (shorter runs, one each, without the fix unless noted):

| Files before the e2e test | `fork` (main) | `spawn` (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| none | 2 passed | 2 passed |
| `test_aiter_mla_uniform_mtp_qo_len.py` | 2 passed | |
| `test_encoder_only_attention_hooks.py` | **2 failed** | |
| `test_encoder_only_attention_hooks.py::test_bert_layers_receive_the_backend` only | **2 failed** | |
| `test_encoder_only_attention_hooks.py`, the other 6 tests | **2 failed** | |
| `test_aiter_mla_uniform_mtp_qo_len.py` + `test_encoder_only_attention_hooks.py` | **2 failed** (`2 failed, 16 passed, 2 skipped in 25.86s`) | **passed** (`18 passed, 2 skipped in 67.46s`) |

```bash
cd /vllm-workspace/tests
pytest -v -s v1/attention/test_aiter_mla_uniform_mtp_qo_len.py v1/attention/test_encoder_only_attention_hooks.py v1/attention/test_encoder_only_attention_hooks_e2e.py
```

Local checks: `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on `tests/utils.py` (ruff 0.17.2, the pre-commit version) pass.

## Details

Root cause: since #67821, when `torch.cuda.is_initialized()` is false, the ROCm memory wait queries memory from a forked one-worker pool so that the pytest process stays HIP-free. But torch is not the only thing that can initialize HIP in that process. After `test_encoder_only_attention_hooks.py` runs, HIP is initialized while torch still reports it uninitialized. The forked child's `torch.cuda.init()` then succeeds, but the next `torch.accelerator.get_memory_info()` raises `hipErrorInvalidValue`, because HIP state does not survive `fork`. The e2e test is the first `VllmRunner` in that process, so it is the test that fails. In shards where other files run first, it passes, for example the daily full CI build [104987](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/104987).

A spawned worker starts from a fresh interpreter and does not inherit the parent's HIP state. The parent never queries HIP, so #67821's benefit is kept. The cost is one worker interpreter that imports `tests.utils` per wait. The measurements above show it is within run-to-run noise compared with the engine startup that follows. I did not narrow down which call in `test_encoder_only_attention_hooks.py` initializes HIP. Both subsets of that file trigger it, and the fix does not depend on the answer.

Limitations: validated on MI355X (gfx950) only, not on the MI300 runners the failing CI job uses. The fix only changes how the worker process starts, and the failure mode does not depend on the GPU architecture.

## Overview

Allow `parallel_config.all2all_backend == "passthrough"` in `HYV4FlashConfig.verify_parallel_config` when Data Parallelism (`dp > 1`) is enabled, unblocking fused-EP MoE backends such as `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` on HY4-Flash DEP deployments.

## Claims

- Update `HYV4FlashConfig.verify_parallel_config` (`vllm/models/hy_v4_flash/configs.py`) to accept both `"allgather_reducescatter"` and `"passthrough"` for `all2all_backend` when `data_parallel_size > 1`, while continuing to reject other unsupported all2all backends.
- Add unit tests in `tests/models/hy_v4/test_flash_dp_config.py` wired into `.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model] Port Mistral Large 4 NVIDIA indexer cache to get_kv_cache_config
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Mistral Large 4 fails to start on NVIDIA GPUs on `main`: every worker crashes at model init because the NVIDIA `MistralIndexerCache` is still abstract. #67984 fixed the AMD copy of this class. This PR makes the same change to the NVIDIA copy.

## Claims

- Fixes the NVIDIA startup crash `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MistralIndexerCache without an implementation for abstract method 'get_kv_cache_config'` for Mistral Large 4.
- No other change in behavior: the indexer cache spec is the same as before, now wrapped in a `KVCacheLayerConfig` under `FullAttentionManager`, as `DeepseekV32IndexerCache` and the AMD `MistralIndexerCache` do.
- `test_indexer_k_cache_write` now builds the real `MistralIndexerCache` on CUDA too, so the `:nvidia: (B200) Mistral Large 4` CI step catches this kind of break.

## Validation

**Regression test:** `test_indexer_k_cache_write` in `tests/models/mistral/test_fused_ops.py` now checks on CUDA, as it already did on ROCm, that the page the model's `MistralIndexerCache.get_kv_cache_config()` requests matches the cache the kernels are tested on. We had no free NVIDIA GPU to run the test itself. We ran its new check (the same calls, without the CUDA kernel part) on CPU in the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-60bd6dd2edd175a1c55fd3488f871e4c3d2ef27d` image:

<details>
<summary>Without fix</summary>

```
TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MistralIndexerCache without an implementation for abstract method 'get_kv_cache_config'
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>With fix</summary>

```
block_size=1: page_size_bytes=132 ok
block_size=16: page_size_bytes=2112 ok
block_size=64: page_size_bytes=8448 ok
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>The CPU check</summary>

```python
import torch
from vllm.config import (CacheConfig, CompilationConfig, CompilationMode, DeviceConfig,
                         VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config)
from vllm.models.mistral.nvidia.indexer import MistralIndexerCache

head_dim = 128
for block_size in (1, 16, 64):
    vllm_config = VllmConfig(device_config=DeviceConfig(device="cpu"), compilation_config=CompilationConfig(mode=CompilationMode.NONE))
    with set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config):
        k_cache = MistralIndexerCache(
            head_dim=head_dim + 4,
            dtype=torch.uint8,
            prefix="indexer.k_cache",
            cache_config=CacheConfig(block_size=block_size),
        )
    spec = k_cache.get_kv_cache_config(vllm_config).spec
    cache_page = torch.zeros(block_size, head_dim + 4, dtype=torch.uint8)
    assert spec.page_size_bytes == cache_page.numel() * cache_page.element_size()
    print(f"block_size={block_size}: page_size_bytes={spec.page_size_bytes} ok")
```
</details>

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check` (v0.17.2) and `typos` (v1.51.1) pass on both changed files.

**End-to-end** on 8x NVIDIA B300, TP=8, image `nightly-60bd6dd2` (both runs also carry the parser-only #63161):

```bash
vllm serve mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B-NVFP4 \
  --tokenizer-mode mistral --config-format mistral --load-format mistral \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len 262144 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser mistral --reasoning-parser mistral \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'
```

Our command also sets sampling defaults, batching limits and KV offloading. None of them touch this code.

<details>
<summary>Without fix: all 8 workers fail at model init</summary>

```
(Worker_TP1 pid=531) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1091]   File ".../vllm/models/mistral/mistral_large4/nvidia/model.py", line 86, in __init__
(Worker_TP1 pid=531) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1091]     self.self_attn = MistralMLAAttention(
(Worker_TP1 pid=531) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1091]   File ".../vllm/models/mistral/nvidia/attention.py", line 129, in __init__
(Worker_TP1 pid=531) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1091]     MistralIndexer(
(Worker_TP1 pid=531) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1091]   File ".../vllm/models/mistral/nvidia/indexer.py", line 146, in __init__
(Worker_TP1 pid=531) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1091]     self.k_cache = MistralIndexerCache(
(Worker_TP1 pid=531) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1091] TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MistralIndexerCache without an implementation for abstract method 'get_kv_cache_config'
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {}
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>With fix: the server starts and serves requests</summary>

```
(Worker_TP0 pid=923) INFO [model_runner.py:449] Model loading took 76.79 GiB memory and 662.359565 seconds
(EngineCore pid=709) INFO [kv_cache_utils.py:1134] GPU KV cache size: 3,336,320 tokens, Maximum concurrency for 262,144 tokens per request: 12.73x
(EngineCore pid=709) INFO [core.py:443] init engine (profile, create kv cache, warmup model) took 784.09 s
INFO:     Application startup complete.
(APIServer pid=1) INFO [loggers.py:339] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 2.3 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 8.8 tokens/s, Running: 0 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, Finished: 1 reqs, ...
(APIServer pid=1) INFO [metrics.py:135] SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 3.39, ...
```
</details>

## Details

**Root cause:** a merge race. #61452 (merged 2026-11-13 04:47 UTC) made `get_kv_cache_config` the abstract KV-cache hook on `AttentionLayerBase` and moved every existing layer to it. #64534 (merged 2026-11-13 15:05 UTC) was written against the old interface. Nothing in vLLM calls `get_kv_cache_spec` any more, so the old method was dead code and the class could not be created.

**Fix:** rename the method in `vllm/models/mistral/nvidia/indexer.py` and return `FullAttentionManager.layer_config(spec)`, as `DeepseekV32IndexerCache` and #67984 do.

**Test:** the page-size check in `test_indexer_k_cache_write` moves out of the ROCm-only branch, so it runs on both platforms. The cache readers check stays ROCm-only.

**CI:** the test runs in the existing `:nvidia: (B200) Mistral Large 4` step (`pytest -v -s models/mistral`). CI cannot run the full 1T-parameter model, so end-to-end coverage is the manual run above.

**Not a duplicate:** no open issue or PR covers the NVIDIA file. #67984 changed only the AMD file, and the open #68061 does not touch the NVIDIA indexer file.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find the cause, write the change and write this description. I reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Turn automatic sharding on by default
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Trunk change: needs line-by-line review (one line in `.buildkite/ci_config.yaml` that changes how every step's shards are decided).

Sets `automatic_shard_default: true`, so the pipeline generator plans shards for every step whose test commands are plain pytest, without a per-step `automatic_shard: true`. The generator support is vllm-project/ci-infra#885. A step opts out with `automatic_shard: false`. A step that can't be split (a script, `cargo`, a fixed hand split) keeps running exactly as it does today.

Main carries 497 `automatic_shard: true` flags today, so for almost every step this changes nothing. After it merges, a new step shards without anyone adding the flag.

This replaces the earlier content of this PR, which predated the generator rework and marked exclusions step by step; those are no longer needed.

## Claims

- No step is added or removed: 390 in a PR build that runs everything, 570 in a nightly.
- Every step that already has the flag is planned as before.
- Zero PR steps change job count. Three nightly steps that are not flagged today start being planned:

| Step | Jobs today → with this | Runs in |
|---|---|---|
| LM Eval Spec Decode | 1 → 3 | nightly |
| its AMD mirror | 1 → 2 | nightly |
| Elastic EP Scaling | 1 → 2 | nightly |

- Every build gets one collapsed annotation, "N jobs ran as one job without a shard plan", listing those jobs and why. Nothing else changes in what people see.

## Validation

- Rendered main's pipeline with the merged generator, switch off and on, as a PR build that runs everything (390 steps, 622 jobs on both sides) and as a nightly (570 steps, 925 → 929 jobs). The three nightly steps above are the only unflagged steps whose job count the switch changes.
- `split_check.py` passes on the PR head (no multi-job step duplicates its suite).
- The switch itself was staged before the generator change merged (#66965, builds 101689 and 101703): sharded jobs ran the same node IDs as main, and jobs that can't be split ran as one job under the annotation.
- Scoped build on an earlier head (https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102675) verified unflagged steps split with no per-step flag and matched main's node IDs (details in the build note on this PR).
- Triggered `/ci run` on this head to post the required `buildkite/ci/pr` status.

## Details

- **Only the switch, the flags stay.** Deleting the 497 now-redundant flags is a follow-up with no behavior change; doing it here would conflict with open PRs.
- **No `automatic_shard: false` is added.** All three nightly steps that start sharding have already been validated sharded; opting any step out later is a one-line change.
- **A new step shards without a validation build.** A test that depends on running after another test will then fail on the PR that adds it. The per-build missed-test check (vllm-project/ci-infra#884) is not merged yet.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][Qwen4Exp] Tune QSA sparse GQA and indexer on gfx942 and gfx950
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follows #62590 and #62589 (both merged). It tunes the two Triton QSA kernels on gfx942 and gfx950:

1. Sparse GQA: pad the head group to 16 rows and use one BF16 launch profile for both archs.
2. Indexer: score only up to the batch's longest sequence, not the whole padded page table.
3. Indexer: use #62589's one-row decode kernel on gfx950 too, with its own tile.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs for "qsa_sparse_paged_attention", "qsa_select_paged_tokens", "QSA indexer"; #57969 pads `BLOCK_M` for gfx11 only (same line, will conflict textually).

## Claims

All against #62590 + #62589. gfx942 is MI325X, gfx950 is MI355X.

- Sparse GQA: geomean 1.57x prefill / 1.65x decode on gfx942, 1.24x / 1.45x on gfx950, never slower by more than 1% (TP1-TP8, 1-16,384 rows).
- Indexer prefill: 1.3-6.5x at 8K-60K context, 8-11x for 1K prompts.
- Indexer decode on gfx950: 2.4x at 32 rows, 1.8x at 128 rows (8K context); gfx942 unchanged.
- Flash-Next FP8 TP2 on MI325X: from 8K up, TTFT 0.96-0.98x (8K/c16 1.02x) and output throughput 1.01-1.03x. 1K/c64 is flat: TTFT 0.96-1.03x and throughput 1.00x over three passes.
- Flash-Next MXFP4 TP2 on MI355X: output throughput 1.01-1.06x in all 10 cells, mean TTFT 0.90-0.96x except 60K/c16-c64 (1.00x, 1.04x).
- GSM8K unchanged; RULER NIAH (single_2) is 1.000 at 64K and 128K on MI325X and MI355X.

## Validation

**Unit tests.** `pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_amd.py` at d4f3bea on MI355X: `101 passed, 17 warnings in 70.23s`.

- `test_qsa_mqa_paged_matches_reference` runs both CDNA versions' one-row profiles at 1 row, at their max rows and one past it.
- `test_qsa_sparse_paged_attention_matches_reference` runs both CDNA versions' profiles, including TP4/TP8 below 32 programs (padded head group), 128/129 programs and 2,048 (single split).
- `test_qsa_select_bounds_columns_to_max_seq_len`: a bound covering the longest request keeps the selection exactly, and a shorter bound drops its top block. It fails if the bound is one column short or ignored (checked by mutation), across three page size and compress ratio cases.

**Kernel evidence.** µs, CUDA-graph replay. Sparse GQA, BF16 K/V, 32K context, #62590 → this PR:

| 1 | 11.3 → 11.3 | 36.1 → 11.1 | 9.4 → 9.4 | 19.7 → 9.0 |
| 32 | 49.4 → 34.8 | 45.4 → 32.2 | 30.6 → 22.4 | 30.8 → 20.0 |

| 16,384 | 4,967 → 3,973 | 7,136 → 3,793 | 3,258 → 2,908 | 3,621 → 2,806 |

Indexer, #62589 → this PR:

| case | gfx942 | gfx950 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| prefill 8 × 1K | 576 → 69 | 750 → 69 |
| prefill 1 × 8K | 732 → 145 | 923 → 143 |
| prefill 16K chunk at 60K | 2,906 → 2,144 | 3,004 → 1,855 |
| decode 32 rows | unchanged | 42.3 → 17.4 |
| decode 128 rows | unchanged | 58.5 → 33.2 |

The indexer uses a 168 × 392-key table. Selections are identical except in gfx950 1 × 8K, where 132 of 8,192 rows differ at exact 0.0 score ties at the top-k boundary.

**End to end.** MI325X, `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` TP2, `nightly-40941f2c`, one repeat with both arms side by side on separate GPU pairs, fixed lengths. Each arm differs from the nightly only in the two AMD QSA files.

| 128K / 1K | 16 | 8,701 / 8,236 / −5.3% | 256 / 264 / +3.1% |

Geomean over the 10 cases: TTFT −4.8%, output throughput +3.3%.

**Accuracy.** GSM8K 5-shot, flexible-extract, MI325X TP2; flips against this PR (0.9689):

| Against | Accuracy | Fixed / broken | Exact McNemar p |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main | 0.9689 | 6 / 6 | 1.00 |
| #62590 + #62589 | 0.9719 | 3 / 7 | 0.34 |

RULER `niah_single_2`, this PR, TP2, 500 samples per length:

| | 64K | 128K |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MI325X, FP8 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| MI355X, MXFP4 | 1.000 | 1.000 |

**Reproduce:**

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CUSTOM_AR=0 \
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 60000 --random-output-len 600 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos --max-concurrency 4 --num-prompts 16
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template \
  --model_args model=Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,max_gen_toks=2048
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --tasks niah_single_2 --apply_chat_template --seed 1234 \
  --metadata '{"max_seq_lengths":[65536,131072]}' --gen_kwargs continue_final_message=True,add_generation_prompt=False \
  --model_args '{"model": "Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8", "tokenizer": "Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8", "base_url": "http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions", "num_concurrent": 8, "tokenized_requests": false}'
```

## Details

- **Sparse GQA:** with BF16 K/V, `tl.dot` with fewer than 16 rows is slow on gfx942 and gfx950, so the TP4/TP8 head groups are padded to 16. From 32 programs up, both archs use `BLOCK_N=16` with enough splits for about 2,048 programs and one warp, or 2 warps at 32-128 programs. On gfx950, 32-128 programs use about 1,024 programs with 4 warps. FP8 K/V is unchanged.
- **Indexer bound:** the logits are `cdiv(max_seq_len, compress_ratio)` columns wide instead of the full table width (65,856 at a 262K `max_model_len`). This is the same bound the NVIDIA indexer uses. Graph capture passes `max_seq_len = max_model_len`, so captured decode is unchanged. Exact ties at the top-k boundary can break differently.
- **One-row decode:** gfx950 uses (128 rows, `BLOCK_N=128`, 2 warps), and gfx942 keeps (32, 32, 4).

Limitations and CI gaps: TP2 e2e on MI325X and MI355X; the kernel sweeps cover TP1-TP8. FP8 K/V profiles were not swept.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Don't treat a finished build left blocked by the test picker as running
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`/ci retry` on #66456 answered "✅ The previous CI build is still running: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/104853" twice (11-23 17:36 and 22:01). That build wasn't running: its 354 script jobs finished, the last at 23:04, and its only unfinished job is the test picker's `:rocket: Upload the picked jobs` (`upload-more-jobs-6`), still `blocked`. Buildkite keeps such a build in state `blocked`, with `finished_at` set, for as long as nobody clicks the picker.

`is_active_build()` returns true for any build that is `blocked` (by state or by the `blocked` flag). Since the "Run more tests" picker, every PR build ends that way, so:

- `/ci retry` after a new push (the new-head path) always says the previous build "is still running".
- `/ci run` on a commit whose build finished says "already running for this commit".

A blocked build now counts as active only while it has unfinished work, i.e. no `finished_at`, or a state such as `failing` that is active on its own. The AMD path, which already ignored blocked builds, is unchanged.

## Test Plan

```
cd .github/workflows/scripts
uv run --no-project --with pytest python -m pytest -q test_run_ci_command.py
```

New cases:
- `is_active_build` is false for a blocked build that has `finished_at` (state `blocked` or `passed`), and true for one without it or one that is `failing`.
- `/ci retry` on a new head creates the filtered build from a finished-but-blocked source build.
- `/ci retry` still waits when the blocked source build has unfinished jobs.

## Test Result

95 passed, 157 subtests passed. Ruff check and format clean.
