commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Stop reloading from the store after a failed load
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

With `kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"`, a failed MooncakeStore load resets `num_computed_tokens` and reschedules the request, and the scheduler clears its failure marker once the receive completes. On the next admission `MooncakeStoreScheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens` queries the store again; if the lookup keeps reporting the hit while the GET keeps failing (e.g. stale metadata for a dead segment), the request bounces between `WAITING` and `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` forever and never falls back to local compute.

P/D connectors (Nixl, Mooncake P/D) are not affected since they clear `do_remote_prefill` after the first pull. `OffloadingConnector` already guards this with a per-request `load_failed` flag; this adds the equivalent to MooncakeStore:

- `update_connector_output` records failed requests, from both `failed_recving` (HMA) and `invalid_block_ids` (mapped through the request's allocated store-group blocks).
- `get_num_new_matched_tokens` reports no store hit for them, so the retry recomputes locally.
- The entry is dropped when the request finishes.

## Test Plan

New unit test `test_failed_load_skips_store_lookup_until_finished` in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py`, parametrized over both failure reporting paths.

## Test Result

CI.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][DeepSeek V4] Keep input IDs on later pipeline stages
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek V4 MegaMoE routing consumes the original token IDs in every decoder layer. Under pipeline parallelism, Model Runner V2 drops `input_ids` on non-first stages, so the text-only `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` fails on the second stage (`AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'to'`).

Since #61016, the runner keeps `input_ids` on later PP stages for models that set `requires_raw_input_tokens`. The vision variant already sets it; this PR sets it on the text-only `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` (NVIDIA backend) as well.

An earlier revision carried `input_ids` through `IntermediateTensors`. Following review, it was replaced by this one-line opt-in to the existing runner mechanism.

Duplicate searches were performed for DeepSeek V4 pipeline-parallel `input_ids` issues and PRs; no matching fix was found.

## Test Plan

- DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP2 + EP + `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, with PP1 / PP2 / PP4.
- GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot) and prompt logprobs on six fixed prompts with `prompt_logprobs: 0`.

## Test Result

Results from @xsxszab on B300, main `da0b6ac221` (see review comment):

| Config | Startup | GSM8K |
|---|---|---|
| PP1, main | serves | 0.951 |
| PP2, main | fails on the second stage | – |
| PP2, main + `requires_raw_input_tokens = True` | serves | 0.949 |
| PP4, main + `requires_raw_input_tokens = True` | serves | 0.946 |

Prompt logprobs for PP2 with the flag match the earlier `IntermediateTensors` approach at all 412 scored positions.

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on the changed file.

## AI assistance disclosure

AI assistance was used to investigate the failure, prepare the patch, and draft this description. The submitter reviewed every changed line and the test evidence before submission.

commits.pr_title: [Benchmark] Time real server starts in vllm bench startup (--serve-cmd)
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`vllm bench startup` builds `LLM` in one process with `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0` and stops its clock when the object exists. That leaves out the API server, the engine-core and worker processes and the first request, which is most of what you wait for when you run `vllm serve`.

This adds `--serve-cmd`. The benchmark launches the server command it is given and times launch to `/health` and launch to the first text of a streamed completion, for the same cold and warm iterations it already has. It is a mode on the existing command, and it launches and stops the server with `ServerProcess` from `vllm bench sweep serve`.

This is the "Startup benchmark" box in #56049 and the measurement #48193 asks for. It adds no per-phase report: that is #49037, and I've tried to stay out of its way. #51143 proposed the same measurement as a separate Rust tool and was closed by its author.

## Claims

- `vllm bench startup --serve-cmd 'vllm serve <model> ...'` reports launch-to-ready and launch-to-first-token for cold and warm starts, with the existing `--num-iters-*` flags and `--output-json`.
- On two B300s at TP2 it measures Qwen3-32B at 109.97 s cold and 67.77 s warm (median of three), against 110.21 s and 67.22 s from an external harness timing the same command in the same Slurm allocation.
- A start only counts if its completion matches the first start's, so a restart that comes up faster and answers differently is reported as a failure, not a speedup.
- Engine arguments passed next to `--serve-cmd` are rejected by name instead of being ignored. Without this, `vllm bench sweep startup` would label its arms differently while running the same server.
- `ServerProcess` gains optional keyword arguments. `vllm bench sweep serve` behaves as before, except that `--port=8100` is now understood as well as `--port 8100`.

## Validation

GPU run: Slurm job on one node, two B300s, `vllm/vllm-openai` nightly at `9c1d45c2`, with this PR's `vllm/benchmarks/startup.py` and `vllm/benchmarks/sweep/server.py` mounted over the wheel's files (neither file changed between `9c1d45c2` and this PR's base). Weights on local NVMe and in page cache. Seconds from launch to the first token:

| Qwen3-32B, TP2, `--max-model-len 4096` | External harness | `vllm bench startup --serve-cmd` |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| First start, empty caches | 110.21 | 109.97 (`--num-iters-cold 1`) |
| Unchanged restart | 67.22 | 67.27, 68.29, 67.77 |

`/health` answered 0.03 to 0.04 s before the first token in every start. Every start returned the same completion and token IDs as the first one, and no server process was left after any of them.

The new test, run with pytest in the same image on one B300:

```
tests/benchmarks/test_bench_startup.py::test_bench_startup_serves_matching_completion_after_restart PASSED
=================== 1 passed, 2 warnings in 85.74s (0:01:25) ===================
```

An earlier revision of this patch, with the same clock and request code and its own launcher, was also run on Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 at TP2: 72.97 s (median of three restarts) against 72.13 s from the harness.

At `e4dfc4f0`, `pytest -q tests/benchmarks/sweep tests/benchmarks/test_plot_filters.py` returned `64 passed in 4.56s` on CPU (62 before this PR; the two new cases are the existing stop test with a grace period). The two files mounted in the GPU run are byte-identical to the ones in that commit.

To reproduce:

```bash
vllm bench startup \
  --serve-cmd 'vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-32B --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 4096 --port 8100' \
  --num-iters-cold 1 --num-iters-warmup 1 --num-iters-warm 3 \
  --output-json startup.json
```

## Details

**Why `--serve-cmd`.** It is the flag `vllm bench sweep serve` already takes, with the same quoting. The benchmark runs the command as given, so what it times is what a user runs, whatever flags or wrapper that is.

**What is timed.** The clock is read immediately before the process is spawned. Ready is the first 200 from `/health`, polled every 50 ms. The first token is the first non-empty text of one greedy `/v1/completions` request (eight tokens), sent as soon as the server is ready. The server's output goes to a log file per start when `--output-json` is set.

**Verified.** A start verifies when its completion finishes normally and its text and token IDs equal those of the first completed start. That is "same as the first start", not "correct". A healthy server can fail it: output that is only empty text or EOS, no `/v1/completions` endpoint, or kernels tuned differently between starts flipping a near-tie. The exit status is then 1 and the timings stay in the per-iteration rows.

**Cold** means what it means today: `cold_startup()` gives the server an empty `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` and empty TorchInductor and Triton caches. Caches that other libraries keep elsewhere follow the environment.

**Stopping.** SIGTERM to the root process, up to 30 s, then SIGKILL to the process group, which is what `RemoteOpenAIServer` does in the tests. A server that had to be killed fails its iteration and ends the run, because the next start could read caches it did not finish writing. Results collected so far are still written.

**Not here.** A per-phase breakdown (#49037), and compilation time, which is not visible from outside the server.

**Overlap.** #60699 changes `is_server_ready` and `wait_until_ready` in the same file. This PR gives `is_server_ready` the same `timeout` parameter, so whichever lands second has a small, mechanical conflict.

One thing I'm unsure about: whether a completion that differs between a cold and a warm start should fail the run by default, as it does here, or only be reported.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Honor DecisionLimits.labeled in /v1/decisions
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`/v1/decisions` ignores `DecisionLimits.labeled` and caps every question at 26 options, even for read strategies that do not score options by label tokens. `/v1/systemone` already honors the flag. Independent fix; no dependencies.

## Claims

- For strategies exposed by `/v1/decisions`, questions honor `max_options` when the strategy reports `labeled=False`, subject to the request schema's 255-choice cap, matching `/v1/systemone`.
- D3 HTTP support is unchanged: `D3Strategy.task == "classify"` is still rejected during Decisions API initialization with 501; the D3 test exercises the serving layer directly.
- Labeled strategies keep the 26-option cap and the same error message.

## Validation

Unit tests (1x GB300 node, nightly wheel of `fdc3364c9` = this branch's parent + the two changed files; `pytest -v -s entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions entrypoints/openai/decisions` in one process, as in CI):

| | this PR | main |
| --- | --- | --- |
| whole suite | 169 passed, 1 failed | 167 passed, 3 failed |
| `test_unlabeled_reads_take_more_choices_than_labels` (new) | passed | failed |
| `test_decisions_serving_unlabeled_choices_exceed_label_limit` (new) | passed | failed |
| `test_backend_rejects_more_choices_than_single_token_labels` (existing, labeled cap) | passed | passed |

The one other failure (`test_structured_decisions_e2e.py::test_request_template_is_rejected_by_default`) fails the same way on unmodified main and is unrelated. `pre-commit run` on the changed files (incl. mypy) passes.

End to end: an 8B bidirectional decision checkpoint served through an out-of-tree `ReadStrategy` with `DecisionLimits(max_questions=64, max_options=512, labeled=False)`; one choice question with N options sent to both endpoints (same option names, descriptions and state text):

| N | main `/v1/decisions` | this PR `/v1/decisions` | `/v1/systemone` | max \|Δp\| decisions vs systemone |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5 | 200 | 200 | 200 | 0.0 |
| 26 | 200 | 200 | 200 | 0.0 |
| 27 | 400 "at most 26 choices" | 200 | 200 | 0.0 |
| 40 | 400 | 200 | 200 | 0.0 |
| 100 | 400 | 200 | 200 | 0.0 |

## Details

Root cause: `make_read_question` (`vllm/entrypoints/openai/decisions/adapters.py`) computed `limit = min(max_options, len(LABELS))` unconditionally, and `OpenAIServingDecisions` did not pass the strategy's `labeled` flag. `build_question` (used by `/v1/systemone`) already does `min(max_options, len(label_set)) if labeled else max_options`. The fix adds `labeled: bool = True` to `make_read_question`, applies the same rule, and passes `self.limits.labeled` from the serving class. `labels=LABELS[: len(options)]` is unchanged; unlabeled strategies do not read `Question.labels` (same as `build_question`).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MLA] Fix race in in-place LSE merge of chunked context
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Clone the prefix LSE before `accumulate_mla_context_chunk` merges a continuation chunk in place. The native `merge_attn_states` kernel can overwrite a head's LSE before all of that head's threads have read it. Fixes the flaky `test_fused_prefill_context_matches_unfused[context_lens1-2]` in [AMD nightly build 15868](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15868/list?jid=01a207da-fa0f-4e4f-9fc8-9c21af0e809a&tab=output). The in-place merge came in with #50613.

## Claims

**Fixes wrong attention output** for tokens merged across a chunk boundary, when a request's context spans two chunks.

**The new test fails on main every time and passes with the fix.**

**Small cost, only on continuation chunks:** `_compute_prefill_context` of the CI test case goes from 282.0 to 288.8 us.

## Validation

1x MI355X (gfx950), `rocm/vllm-ci:test-deps-rocm-aece323e26e87ef2`, base `ee1d07c7b2`. "main" is the same tree without the `.clone()`.

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/v1/attention/test_mla_context_chunks.py::test_continuation_merge_matches_an_out_of_place_merge
```

| Check | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| New test | failed 3 of 3 | passed 5 of 5 (1.75 s) |
| CI test comparison, once per fresh process | 7 of 80 failed | 0 of 80 failed |
| `test_mla_context_chunks.py`, `test_rocm_aiter_mla_prefill_fusions.py`, `test_mla_prefill_flash_attn.py`, `test_merge_attn_states.py` | | all passed (15, 12, 2598) |

<details>
<summary>New test output</summary>

```
# main
E           Mismatched elements: 3310 / 294912 (1.1%)
E           Greatest absolute difference: 1.921875 at index (37, 5, 154) (up to 1e-05 allowed)
======================== 1 failed, 17 warnings in 2.30s ========================
# this PR
1.75s call     tests/v1/attention/test_mla_context_chunks.py::test_continuation_merge_matches_an_out_of_place_merge
======================== 1 passed, 17 warnings in 2.18s ========================
```
</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** `output_lse` and `prefix_lse` are the same slice. The kernel gives each thread 8 elements of a head and only the head's first thread writes the merged LSE. With D=192 (V padded for the `FLASH_ATTN` prefill backend) a head needs 24 threads, so some heads span two 128-thread blocks. If one block writes the LSE before the other reads it, the second block merges with the wrong weight. It depends on block order, so in CI it failed 1 time in 46 runs; the new test forces it with a busy side stream.

**Why this fix.** Before #50613 this merge used separate buffers, as `rocm_aiter_fa.py` still does. Only the LSE needs a copy, since each thread reads and writes only its own part of `output`. No other `merge_attn_states` caller aliases the LSE.

**CI coverage.** The new test runs in the V1 Attention steps (H100, B200, MI300, MI355). I verified it on MI355 only.

AI assistance was used for this PR.

## Overview Optimized `_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1` in `vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_decode_attention.py` by co-scheduling head blocks on `grid[0]` for L2 KV cache locality and loading `K_Buffer` in row-major `[BLOCK_N, BLOCK_DMODEL]` layout for 128-bit vectorized coalescing and bank-conflict-free shared-memory writes. Prior to this PR, `_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1` scheduled grid as `(batch, head_groups, NUM_KV_SPLITS)`. in MLA, the latent KV head is same for all query heads - but for this grid, for all query head_groups were being scheduled in strided manner since grid scheduler traverses batch dimension first. Secondly, `K_Buffer` was being loaded from global memory with `[BLOCK_DMODEL, BLOCK_N]` as page tile where `BLOCK_DMODEL` being contiguous dimension was being loaded in strided manner ## Claims * **Consistent `TRITON_MLA` decode kernel speedups across GPU architectures** (18 `(batch, seq_len)` configurations, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite` geometry): * **NVIDIA H100:** **1.06x–1.71x** speedup (`1.49x–1.71x` across long-context and batched decode shapes). * **NVIDIA A100:** **1.05x–1.47x** speedup across batched and long-context decode shapes (`1.41x–1.47x` at `bs=128`). * **NVIDIA L40S:** **1.06x–1.38x** speedup across all 18 tested shapes. * **H100 Nsight Compute on `64q1s8k`:** * **L2 cache hit rate** increased from **55% -> 74%**. * **Shared-memory store bank conflicts** eliminated (`4.4-way` / `8.06%` penalty -> **0**), reducing dynamic shared memory per block from **63.49 KB -> 56.32 KB**. * **Minimal, portable diff with full feature parity:** ~15-line kernel/launcher diff preserving FP8 KV cache dequantization, Sliding Window Attention (`SLIDING_WINDOW`), GQA/MHA grouped paths, and Stage-2 reduction. ## Validation ### 1. Nsight Compute Hardware Metrics (H100, `64q1s8k`) | NCU Metric (`_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1`) | `main` (`[512, 32]`, `grid[0]=batch`) | This Branch (`[32, 512]`, `grid[0]=head`) | Improvement | | :--- | ---: | ---: | :--- | | **Kernel Duration** | `2.21 ms` | **`1.42 ms`** | **1.55x faster** | | **L2 Cache Hit Rate** | `~55%` | **`~74%`** | **+19 pp** | | **Shared Store Bank Conflicts** | `4.4-way` (`8.06%` penalty) | **`0`** | **Eliminated** | | **Dynamic Shared Memory / Block** | `63.49 KB` | **`56.32 KB`** | **-7.17 KB / CTA** |
End-to-End Serving Benchmarks (H100, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, FP8 KV Cache) Validated with `vllm bench sweep serve` (`--attention-backend TRITON_MLA --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `--dataset-name random --seed 42`) comparing `main` (`9b088c6667cbb9cce3eaa5ad937548aad36e8e7e`) vs. this branch: *(Note: `DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` uses 16 query heads, so `NUM_HEAD_BLOCKS = 1`; the `grid[0]` L2 head-block co-scheduling gain applies on 128-head MLA models such as DeepSeek-V2/V3/R1 and multi-head-block GQA models, while `DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` validates end-to-end FP8 stability and zero regressions up to 100k context.)* | `max_num_seqs` | `max_model_len` | `max_concurrency` | `random_input_len` | `random_output_len` | Mean TPOT `main` (ms) | Mean TPOT This Branch (ms) | Median TPOT `main` (ms) | Median TPOT This Branch (ms) | Throughput `main` (tok/s) | Throughput This Branch (tok/s) | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 64 | 16,384 | 64 | 4,096 | 128 | 34.80 | **34.67** | 37.03 | **36.86** | 1,561.09 | **1,564.55** | | 128 | 32,768 | 64 | 4,096 | 128 | 36.42 | **36.33** | 38.68 | **38.58** | 1,501.62 | **1,505.91** | | 64 | 102,400 | 32 | 50,000 | 128 | 170.23 | **170.17** | 199.64 | 199.70 | 101.49 | **101.52** | | 64 | 102,400 | 16 | 80,000 | 128 | 202.71 | 204.51 | 250.57 | 252.50 | 50.22 | 49.89 | | 64 | 102,400 | 16 | 100,000 | 128 | 243.82 | **242.62** | 285.28 | 288.15 | 34.92 | **35.03** |
## Details ### Root Cause Profiling `_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1` on H100 revealed two hardware bottlenecks: 1. **L2 Cache Thrashing Across Head Blocks:** With `grid = (batch, NUM_HEAD_BLOCKS, NUM_KV_SPLITS)`, CUDA launches CTAs along `grid[0]` (`batch`) first. For 128-head MLA (`NUM_HEAD_BLOCKS = 8`), all 8 head blocks for a given `(batch, kv_split)` share the exact same compressed KV cache pages (`cur_kv_head = 0`), but scheduling across `batch` first evicted those KV pages from L2 before the remaining head blocks for the same request ran. 2. **Uncoalesced Global KV Loads & Shared-Memory Bank Conflicts:** Loading `K_Buffer` in transposed `[BLOCK_DMODEL, BLOCK_N]` (`[512, 32]`) layout placed the strided token axis (`stride_buf_kbs`) on the inner warp-coalescing dimension. Adjacent threads jumped across separate token rows, yielding `21.3 / 32` byte sector utilization (`27%` excessive global sectors), forcing an in-register transpose with `4.4-way` shared-memory bank conflicts, and requiring `v = tl.trans(k)` on the MLA path. ### Design Decisions & Tradeoffs * **Co-schedule head blocks on `grid[0]`:** Swapping `grid` to `(NUM_HEAD_BLOCKS, batch, NUM_KV_SPLITS)` schedules all `NUM_HEAD_BLOCKS` sharing a KV slice concurrently on the SMs, raising L2 hit rates from `~55%` to `~74%` without altering output indexing or determinism. * **Row-major `[BLOCK_N, BLOCK_DMODEL]` KV loads:** Loading `k` and `kpe` with contiguous `offs_d[None, :]` on the inner dimension enables 128-bit vectorized loads (`LDG.E.128`), writes directly into native `K`-major shared-memory layouts for `tl.dot(q, tl.trans(k.to(q.dtype)))` without bank conflicts, and eliminates `tl.trans(k)` when `IS_MLA=True` (`v = k`). * **Scope:** Kept strictly to Stage-1 grid order and `K_Buffer` load layout so the existing two-stage reduction (`_fwd_kernel_stage2`), batch-invariant deterministic reduction order, and cross-platform support (CUDA, ROCm, XPU) remain intact with minimal code churn. ## Comments I dont have enough compute to test the kernel in E2E model like DSv3, etc. I tried benchmarking DSv2 Lite, but it only has 16 query heads due to which the perf delta was neglibible. I would appreciate if someone could test a bigger model E2E with this kernel patched up. Also appreciate kernel level and E2E benchmarking on other hardware (AMD, etc) that this triton MLA backend supports. This PR description was written using AI assistance and every claim is verified by the author. All the benchmarking and profiling was done by the author

[Deprecation][Quantization] Deprecate the TorchAO backend
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

first step of #69030: deprecate the torchao quantization backend, to be removed in v0.37.

## Claims

- `quantization="torchao"` logs a deprecation warning (once per process) that names v0.37 and links #69030.
- the torchao docs page and the quantization index mark the backend deprecated and point to online quantization or compressed-tensors, gptq, awq and fp8 checkpoints.
- no other behavior change.

## Validation

a100, main 1f41d0fb3 + this diff (unchanged on current main):

```python
LLM("facebook/opt-125m", quantization="torchao",
    hf_overrides={"quantization_config_dict_json": json.dumps(config_to_dict(
        Int4WeightOnlyConfig(group_size=128, int4_packing_format="tile_packed_to_4d")))})
```
```
(MainProcess) WARNING [torchao.py:143] The TorchAO quantization backend is deprecated and will be removed in v0.37. See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/69030 for alternatives.
(EngineCore) WARNING [torchao.py:143] The TorchAO quantization backend is deprecated and will be removed in v0.37. See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/69030 for alternatives.
generated: ' the capital of the French Republic. It'
```

no new test: the change only adds a log line and docs.

## Details

- the warning sits in `TorchAOConfig.__init__`, so it covers online quantization and torchao checkpoints; `warning_once` dedups the per-module configs that `ModuleFqnToConfig` builds.
- v0.36 adds `torchao` to `DEPRECATED_QUANTIZATION_METHODS`; v0.37 removes the backend (#69030).

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode][HY4] Allow DFly on any compressed-tensors target scheme (NVFP4)
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Let HY4 DFly run on compressed-tensors targets regardless of their layer scheme, enabling speculative decoding for [RedHatAI/Hy4-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/Hy4-NVFP4).

## Claims

- DFly accepts compressed-tensors HY4 targets with any layer scheme, rejecting only a `kv_cache_scheme` or non-empty transforms.
- An empty `transform_config: {}`, as serialized by compressed-tensors, is treated as no transforms.
- Draft layers are BF16 or blockwise W8A8 FP8, checked exactly.
- HY4 Flash's own checkpoint validation is unchanged.

## Validation

### Unit tests

```
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dfly_quantization.py -q
```

### End to end on the full 770B model (4x B300, TP4), at `fc56c61ae0`

### Coverage limits

- Target schemes other than NVFP4 and FP8 are covered only at config validation.
- DFly with image or video inputs on NVFP4 is unverified.
- CI cannot hold the 770B checkpoint, so end-to-end coverage is manual.
- The Read the Docs failure is also on main: the same 15 `docs/training/weight_updates` link warnings, starting at #69248.

## Details

**Root cause.** `adapt_draft_model_config` applied HY4 Flash's list of FP8 and MXFP4 checkpoint formats to every DFly target. DFly shares the target's MLA KV cache, indexer top-k, embedding and LM head, and does not depend on how the other layers are quantized. KV spec compatibility and BF16 embedding and head are already checked when the draft is loaded.

**Design.** For compressed-tensors, scheme support is left to the target model. Native FP8 checkpoints keep their existing check. Draft layers get their own exact check, matching what the draft loader reads.

**Out of scope.** Draft quantization beyond FP8: the DFly loader infers FFN width from `.weight` shapes and expects BF16 or FP8 dtypes, and the drafter is only 3.3B parameters.

**Related PRs.** I found no open PR for compressed-tensors NVFP4 targets with DFly.

- #68387 adds a separate `modelopt_fp4` bypass for HY4 Flash in the same function.
- #68839 copies the `num_bits`-only draft check into an AMD drafter, which will need the same exact check once this lands.
